## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Users could point audio transcription at private endpoints they do not fully trust.
  - Mitigation: The private-network exception is explicit, audio-only, disabled by default, documented as trusted-endpoint-only, and covered by schema/runtime tests.

## Summary
- add centralized no-op sentinel detection for silent heartbeat/system-event replies
- suppress exact `HEARTBEAT_OK`, `NO_REPLY`, `NO_NEW_AUDIO`, and `SESSION_WATCHDOG_OK` outputs before delivery
- keep meaningful relayable exec summaries deliverable without moving cron events out of heartbeat-mode ack suppression
- preserve newer heartbeat prefix/model-selection behavior after rebasing onto current `origin/main`

Fixes #73149.

## Real behavior proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Heartbeat/system-event handoffs could visibly deliver no-op sentinel replies such as exact `HEARTBEAT_OK`, while still needing to deliver meaningful exec/system-event summaries.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout for PR #73785 on Linux/Node 22 after rebasing onto current `origin/main` at `3de97057d0`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran `node --import tsx tmp/pr73785-runtime-proof.mjs` from the patched checkout. The script imported the patched `runHeartbeatOnce`, used the real in-process system-event queue, registered the channel plugin send path with outbound capture, seeded a real file-backed session store, and exercised both cron-event and exec-event paths.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal output copied from the after-fix proof command:

target.body:
## What

Adds an RFC + two companion design docs proposing **`@openclaw/call-sdk`** — a provider-agnostic real-time call SDK — and its binding into OpenClaw's `ChannelPlugin` model.

The three docs are intentionally split so each can be reviewed independently:

| File | What |
|---|---|
| [`docs/refactor/call-sdk-rfd.mdx`](https://github.com/visionik/clawdis/blob/rfc/call-sdk/docs/refactor/call-sdk-rfd.mdx) | RFC summary: goal, non-goals, proposed interface sketch, three hard tradeoffs. Entry point that links to the two companion docs. |
| [`docs/refactor/call-sdk-design.mdx`](https://github.com/visionik/clawdis/blob/rfc/call-sdk/docs/refactor/call-sdk-design.mdx) | Portable SDK API design: `Call`, `CallTransport`, `CallTap` and built-in tap kinds (`InferenceTap`, `RecordingTap`, `CaptionTap`, `IVRTap`, `TransformTap`, `MixerTap`, `TestTap`), `MediaFrame` v1→v2 plan, fan-out / `AbortSignal` as v1 core, lifecycle observability events, v1 / v1.1 / v2 / later scope split, worked examples, phased roadmap. |
| [`docs/refactor/call-sdk-channel-binding.mdx`](https://github.com/visionik/clawdis/blob/rfc/call-sdk/docs/refactor/call-sdk-channel-binding.mdx) | OpenClaw-side binding: `capabilities.call`, `ChannelPlugin.call: ChannelCallAdapter`, the load-bearing "channels never tap" guardrail (enforced at types / runtime / PR docs), authority/trust boundary between channels and tap-attaching code, two-axes / two-registries split, session-key conventions with `:call:<callId>`, `channel-call-inbound` dispatch helpers, single-connection contract, real-world capability matrix, 8-phase migration path. |

You can also browse all three in the [Files changed tab](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/73606/files).

## Why

OpenClaw handles dozens of messaging channels uniformly today. Real-time calls are not — every transport (WhatsApp calling, the in-progress Google Meet integration, Twilio voice) has its own ad-hoc wiring, no shared `Call` lifecycle, no standard way to attach STT/TTS, no recording, no captions. Every new transport reinvents the same patterns.

This RFC proposes the missing shared layer: a portable `@openclaw/call-sdk` exposing `Call` (per-call lifecycle and media surface) and `CallTap` (anything that consumes or produces media on a call), plus a thin OpenClaw binding (`ChannelPlugin.call: ChannelCallAdapter`) so a single channel package per platform can own both messaging and calls cleanly.

## Three hard tradeoffs (decided)

1. **`Buffer` v1, `MediaFrame` v2.** Ship `AsyncIterable<Buffer>` now to unblock the abstractions; design `MediaFrame` (codec / sample-rate / sequence / track / EOS / error) against real codec needs in v2.
2. **Multi-tap composition over single-bridge.** Many `CallTap`s per call, independent. Requires fan-out + `AbortSignal` cancellation to be boringly correct in v1 core, not v1.1 polish — otherwise detach leaks pipelines.
3. **Policy lives in the host, not the SDK.** `attachTap(call, tap)` is a plain function. OpenClaw wraps it as `core.attachTap(...)` under RBAC; the SDK exposes only attach/detach observability events for hosts to wire consent, audit, and recording-disclosure on top.

## Scope of this PR

**Docs only.** No code, no package added. The RFC asks for review of the design before any implementation begins; companion docs spell out the v1 / v1.1 / v2 / later split so reviewers can see the implementation-phase shape without that work being part of this PR.

## Open questions worth surfacing at RFD level

- Should `messaging` become optional on `ChannelPlugin` so call-only platforms (Meet, PSTN) are first-class? (Recommended: yes.)
- Should the plugin-sdk module path be `channel-call` (matches the renamed cap and SDK) or stay `channel-voice` (matches existing `realtime-voice` registry vocabulary)? (Recommended: `channel-call`.)

## External draft references

These docs were synthesized from in-progress drafts; gists kept until the RFD is merged for reviewers who want the change history:

- Call-SDK design gist: https://gist.github.com/visionik/e95177cc29fe5f9b8d7bb983635a520c
- Channel-plugin design gist: https://gist.github.com/visionik/6d27c758552403ea4b4641c72d73ebda

---

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): resolve 200K context window for Claude 3.x and unlisted Anthropic Bedrock variants
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts` only listed a handful of Anthropic models in `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS`. Common Bedrock IDs such as `anthropic.claude-3-opus-20240229-v1:0`, `anthropic.claude-3-sonnet-20240229-v1:0`, and `anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-2024{0620,1022}-v{1,2}:0` fell through to `defaults.contextWindow` (32K by default), so prompts well below the model's actual 200K window tripped context-overflow precheck and triggered auto-compaction restart loops.
- Why it matters: every Bedrock customer using a Claude 3.x base model that wasn't already enumerated saw the gateway's in-memory model registry advertise 32K and refuse prompts the model could otherwise serve.
- What changed: backfill the missing Claude 3 / 3.5 / Opus 4 base entries at 200K, then add a small `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FAMILIES` table with an `^anthropic\.claude-(3|4)` regex so unlisted future variants and region-prefixed inference profiles (`us.anthropic.claude-*`, `jp.anthropic.claude-*`, etc.) default to 200K. Explicit table entries still win for higher-tier (1M) Claude rows.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no other vendor families. The `defaultContextWindow` config knob is untouched. Inference-profile prefix stripping logic and existing strict matches are unchanged.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] amazon-bedrock plugin (provider discovery)

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #73328
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause

- Root cause: `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` was a hand-maintained map and missed the Claude 3 / 3.5 base IDs that most users encounter on Bedrock. There was no family-level fallback, so any unmatched model fell through to `resolveDefaultContextWindow` (32K default).
- Missing detection / guardrail: no test verified the family-level resolution; existing tests only cover Claude 3.7 / 4.x rows that happened to be in the map.
- Contributing context: AWS does not expose token-limit metadata via `ListFoundationModelsCommand`, so any unmatched model gets the conservative default.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`
- Scenarios the test locks in:
  - Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 (`anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0`) resolves to 200K via the explicit table entry.
  - An unlisted future Claude 3 variant (`anthropic.claude-3-future-preview-v9:0`) resolves to 200K via the `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FAMILIES` fallback rather than 32K.
  - The same family fallback works for region-prefixed inference profiles (`us.anthropic.claude-3-future-preview-v9:0`).
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the bug surface is "missing entry / no fallback in `resolveKnownContextWindow`". The new tests pin both the table backfill and the family fallback, including the inference-profile prefix path.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Bedrock-discovered Claude 3.x models now report 200K context windows in the gateway's in-memory model registry instead of 32K.
- Bedrock-discovered Anthropic models with IDs not listed in `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` default to 200K via family fallback instead of 32K.
- No other providers are affected.

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

## Repro + Verification

### Steps

1. Configure a Bedrock provider with default discovery and a Claude 3.5 Sonnet (or any unlisted Claude 3.x) model.
2. Boot the gateway and inspect the in-memory model registry / `/health/deep`.
3. Send a prompt totalling ~16K input tokens.

### Expected

- `contextWindow` reported as 200000 for `anthropic.claude-*` Bedrock models, no context-overflow precheck triggered for the 16K prompt.

### Actual (before fix)

- `contextWindow=32000`; the 16K prompt is treated as nearly full and triggers `[context-overflow-precheck] estimatedPromptTokens=16300 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=15616` → `Auto-compaction failed.*Restarting session`.

## Evidence

- Static reproduction is provided by the new unit tests in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`. Live Bedrock validation requires AWS credentials and is left to CI / downstream verification.

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: TypeScript clean on touched files; new tests added next to existing `discovery.test.ts` Claude/Sonnet suite.
- Edge cases checked: explicit table entries still win (e.g. Claude Sonnet 4.6 @ 1M), region-prefixed inference profiles route through stripping then family fallback, non-Claude families (Llama, Mistral, etc.) untouched.
- What I did NOT verify: a live Bedrock call with AWS credentials; full `pnpm check` / `pnpm test` was not exercised locally, leaving CI as the verification surface.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes — existing explicit table entries are unchanged. Only previously-incorrect 32K resolutions become 200K.
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: a non-Anthropic Bedrock model id happens to start with `anthropic.claude-3` or `anthropic.claude-4`.
  - Mitigation: AWS's Bedrock model id namespace is provider-prefixed (`anthropic.`), so this regex is well-scoped to the Claude family. The explicit map still takes precedence and any future tier-bump (e.g. another 1M variant) just needs another explicit entry.

target.title: feat(exec): inject OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID env vars for child processes
target.body:
## Summary
Inject `OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY` and `OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID` environment variables into child processes spawned by the exec tool, allowing scripts and skills to reliably identify the current session and agent without relying on model parameter passing.

Supersedes #68859 with full coverage including node-host execution, regression tests, and docs updates.

Closes #66705

## Problem
Currently, skills and scripts executed via exec have no reliable way to determine which session or agent they belong to. While the model can pass these identifiers as parameters, this approach is prone to hallucination errors where the model may provide incorrect values.

This blocks workflows where a child process needs to register a callback or webhook that routes back to the originating session.

## Solution
Automatically inject `OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY` and `OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID` into the environment of child processes spawned by exec, across all execution paths.

### Changes

**Core injection:**
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts` — inject both vars in `runExecProcess` (`shellRuntimeEnv`)
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts` — inject both vars in `shellRuntimeEnv` after sanitization for `host=node` execution
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts` — pass `agentId` through gateway allowlist path

**Type updates:**
- Added `agentId?: string` to `runExecProcess` opts type

**Documentation:**
- `docs/help/environment.md` — document both new env vars
- `docs/tools/exec.md` — note session/agent injection for all exec hosts

**Tests:**
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts` — 6 new tests covering gateway injection, user env override prevention, and empty-string clearing semantics
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — updated sanitizer allowlist test to verify trusted var injection
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts` — removed stale test (gateway no longer injects vars into `requestedEnv`)

## Testing
- [x] Local gateway execution (host=gateway)
- [x] Sandbox execution (host=sandbox) — covered by shared shellRuntimeEnv path
- [x] PTY mode (pty=true) — covered by shared shellRuntimeEnv path
- [x] Node-host execution (host=node) — unit tests in invoke-system-run.test.ts
- [x] Override semantics — user env cannot override trusted values
- [x] Clearing semantics — empty string when no agent/session defaults provided

## Usage Example
```python
import os
session_key = os.environ.get("OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY")
agent_id = os.environ.get("OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID")
```

## Backward Compatibility
Fully backward compatible:
- Variables always set (empty string when not available), avoiding stale-value issues
- Trusted values override any user-provided env overrides with the same names
- No existing behavior changed

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Inject OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID environment variables into exec child processes so skills and scripts can reliably identify their session and agent without relying on model parameter passing.

**Real environment tested**: OpenClaw 2026.4.2, macOS arm64, gateway mode

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
1. Built and ran OpenClaw gateway with the patched code
2. Created a minimal test skill at workspace/skills/test-env-injection/ that prints both environment variables
3. Executed the skill script via the exec tool within a main agent session
4. Captured the console output

**Evidence after fix**:
```bash
$ python3 ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/test-env-injection/test.py
agent:main:2
main
```

**Observed result after fix**: Both OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID are correctly injected into the exec child process environment. The output matches the expected session key (agent:main:2) and agent id (main).

**What was not tested**: Node-host (host=node) execution path was not tested in a real multi-node setup; only unit tests cover this path.

## Problem

The exec-approvals symlink hardening from #72377 only relaxed the restriction on the `OPENCLAW_HOME` root itself, so a symlinked `~/.openclaw` immediate child of a real home directory still trips `assertNoSymlinkPathComponents()`:

\`\`\`
Refusing to traverse symlink in exec approvals path: /Users/funjim/.openclaw
\`\`\`

This breaks \`openclaw exec-policy preset yolo\` (and every other exec-policy command) for users who manage their OpenClaw config via GNU Stow, chezmoi, or any other dotfile-managed setup that exposes \`~/.openclaw → ~/dotfiles/openclaw/.openclaw\`.

## Fix

Allow EXACTLY ONE trusted symlink hop at the immediate child of the trusted home root, gated by the same hardening intent as #64050 / #72377:

1. Only the immediate child of the trusted root may be a symlink (deeper symlinks inside the resolved tree remain rejected).
2. The symlink target's realpath must be owned by the current effective user (\`process.geteuid()\`).
3. The symlink target must not be group- or other-writable (mode bits \`0o022\`).
4. After consuming the trusted hop, traversal continues from the realpath target with the original per-segment symlink rejection — a second symlink anywhere below is still rejected.

Permissive on platforms without \`process.geteuid\` (Windows), where the OS ACL model already differs.

\`ensureDir()\` is taught to accept a \`dir\` whose \`lstatSync\` reports a symlink, but only after re-asserting the realpath target is a directory — \`assertNoSymlinkPathComponents()\` already vetted ownership/perms.

## Tests

- **New**: \`accepts a symlinked ~/.openclaw immediate child of the trusted home\` — constructs the exact GNU Stow layout from the issue and verifies the file lands at the realpath target.
- **Updated**: \`refuses to traverse symlinked approvals components below a symlinked home\` — now constructs an unsafe (group-writable) symlink target so the deeper-symlink rejection intent of #72377 is still exercised. The original test became implicitly the same scenario as the new accept-test once the trusted-hop relaxation landed; making the target unsafe keeps the rejection branch under test.

All 18 \`exec-approvals-store\` tests pass; \`pnpm tsgo:test\` clean.

## Diff

+92 / -3 across 2 production files + 1 test file + CHANGELOG.

## Refs

- Original hardening: #64050
- Replaced PR (broader fix): #64663
- Merged narrow replacement: #72377
- This PR strictly broadens #72377 in the safe direction the issue describes.

target.title: fix(mcp): reject mixed command+url transport config (#72111)
target.body:
Closes #72111.

## Problem

When an MCP server config carries **both** a non-empty `command` and a non-empty `url` (e.g. a streamable-http endpoint plus a `command`/`args` pair), the runtime silently picks stdio and drops the HTTP transport. The user sees:

```
MCP server connection timed out after 30000ms
```

The spawned child never speaks JSON-RPC over stdio because the user actually wanted the streamable-http endpoint. The clawsweeper bot triaged this and recommended early rejection over silent fallback.

## Root cause

`resolveMcpTransportConfig` in `src/agents/mcp-transport-config.ts` resolves the stdio launch first when `command` is set, regardless of whether `url` is also set. The 30s timeout that follows is the user-visible symptom; the silent fallback at config-resolution time is the real bug.

## Reproducer

In `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`:

```json
{
  \"mcp\": {
    \"servers\": {
      \"broken\": {
        \"command\": \"node\",
        \"args\": [\"something.js\"],
        \"url\": \"https://my-mcp.example.com/mcp\"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Run OpenClaw → the `broken` server hangs, then errors with `MCP server connection timed out after 30000ms`. There is no clue in the logs about *which* transport was actually attempted.

## Fix

Reject the ambiguous shape early with a clear diagnostic that names the offending server and the requested transport hint, matching the file's existing \"skipped server X because Y\" diagnostic style and the clawsweeper bot's \"Best possible solution\":

> reject mixed `command` + `url`/HTTP transport configs early with a clear diagnostic and docs/test alignment. The current silent stdio precedence should not remain the user-visible timeout path.

Implementation: when `command` and a non-whitespace `url` are both present, log the warning, return `null` (caller already handles `null` as \"skip this server\"), and let the user fix their config.

Pure stdio configs (no `url`) and pure HTTP configs (no `command`) are unaffected. **Whitespace-only `url`** strings continue to be treated as \"no url\" so stdio still wins, matching the existing trimming in `mcp-stdio.ts`.

Diff: **+17** lines in `mcp-transport-config.ts`, **+52** in tests.

## Verification

```
pnpm vitest run src/agents/mcp-transport-config.test.ts
# 11 passed (7 original + 4 new)

pnpm check
# 0 errors, 0 warnings; all policy guards green
```

## Tests added (4 new)

1. **Mixed config + transport hint** → resolution returns `null`; warning lists both `command` and `url` and the requested transport.
2. **Mixed config without explicit transport hint** → still rejected; warning is informative.
3. **Whitespace-only `url` paired with real `command`** → resolution returns stdio (mirrors `mcp-stdio.ts` trimming).
4. **Sanitized transport in warning** → diagnostic does not leak full URL secrets / query strings.

## Risk notes

- **Behavior change is user-visible**: configs that used to silently fall back to stdio when both `command`+`url` were set now get rejected outright (server skipped, no spawn). That is the bot-blessed shape and matches the issue, but anyone relying on the silent fallback (unlikely — it was the bug) will see a behavior shift on upgrade.
- Did NOT touch `src/agents/mcp-stdio.ts` even though the bot's evidence cites it; the rejection is cleaner at the transport-config layer where both fields are visible together.
- PR collision check: 8 open MCP-related PRs in the repo (#66542, #69417, #69039, #65574, #62134, #64316, #62160, #60005); none touch `mcp-transport-config.ts` validation logic for the mixed shape. Safe to land independently.

target.title: fix(models): default input=[text,image] for vision-capable explicit-only models
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #71921.

When a user's `openclaw.json` contains a static model catalog for a provider (e.g. `amazon-bedrock`) and an entry omits the `input` field, `mergeProviderModels` previously returned that entry unchanged whenever discovery had no matching model to inherit from. Downstream `modelSupportsImages` (`dist/images-CzeTciMv.js`) reads `model.input?.includes("image") ?? false` — so `input === undefined` is silently treated as **text-only**, permanently breaking image attachments.

The full chain that produces this state in the wild:

1. `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts` imports from `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock`. That package is declared in the extension's `package.json` with `stageRuntimeDependencies: true` and is staged into `~/.openclaw/plugin-runtime-deps/.../node_modules/` on first boot after install/upgrade.
2. If OpenClaw resolves the amazon-bedrock catalog **before** runtime-deps staging completes, the import throws, discovery silently catches it, and returns no models.
3. In that empty-discovery state, a **static catalog** gets persisted into the user's `openclaw.json` for `models.providers.amazon-bedrock.models` — entries carrying `id`, `name`, `contextWindow`, `maxTokens`, but no `input`.
4. On subsequent boots, even after `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock` is installed and discovery works correctly, the user still carries that frozen static catalog. `mergeProviderModels` preserves each explicit entry verbatim when there's no matching implicit (discovery) entry, so `input` stays `undefined`.
5. User-visible effect: "Model does not support images" on every Bedrock Claude model, permanently, until the user manually edits `openclaw.json` or `~/.openclaw/agents/*/agent/models.json` to add `input: ["text", "image"]`.

## The fix

Teach `mergeProviderModels` to recognize vision-capable model ID patterns (Claude 3.5+/4.x, GPT-4o / 4.1 / 5 / o-series, Gemini 1.5+, Llama 3.2+ / 4.x vision families) and default `input: ["text", "image"]` when the user's explicit entry omits it and discovery has no match. Explicit entries that already specify `input` (including `input: ["text"]` to opt out of vision) are preserved unchanged, as are entries whose IDs don't match a known vision family.

This makes the merge behaviour "fail safe" for modern multimodal model families: if the user's static catalog is stale or incomplete, vision still works out of the box.

## What this does **not** attempt to fix

Three related issues from #71921 that felt out of scope for this PR — happy to follow up separately if maintainers want:

1. **Bundle `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock` directly** instead of staging via runtime-deps, to eliminate the first-boot race that seeds the stale static catalog in the first place.
2. **Refresh explicit catalogs when discovery later succeeds**, so stale entries don't linger forever.
3. **Add unknown-field warnings** in `planOpenClawModelsJson` when a static catalog is persisted without `input` for a model the provider could discover dynamically.

## Tests

New file: `src/agents/models-config.merge.explicit-input-default.test.ts`

- ✅ Defaults Claude Opus 4.x explicit-only entries to `[text, image]`
- ✅ Defaults Sonnet 4.x and Haiku 4.x explicit-only entries
- ✅ Defaults GPT-4o and Gemini 1.5+ families
- ✅ Preserves explicit `input: ["text"]` opt-out overrides
- ✅ Leaves non-vision / pre-vision model families (Titan embeddings, Claude 2, custom text-only) with `input` undefined
- ✅ Still inherits from implicit discovery when both catalogs contain the same model ID

All 6 tests pass locally. Existing `model-catalog.test.ts` and `models-config.*.test.ts` pass without regression.

## Reproduction / user workaround

Workaround for users hitting this before the fix ships:

```bash
python3 - << 'PY'
import json, pathlib
for p in pathlib.Path.home().glob('.openclaw/agents/*/agent/models.json'):
    d = json.loads(p.read_text())
    for m in d.get('providers',{}).get('amazon-bedrock',{}).get('models', []):
        mid = m.get('id','').lower()
        if any(k in mid for k in ['claude-opus-4','claude-sonnet-4','claude-haiku-4','claude-3-5','claude-3-7']):
            if 'image' not in m.get('input', []):
                m['input'] = ['text','image']
    p.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=2))

p = pathlib.Path.home() / '.openclaw' / 'openclaw.json'
d = json.loads(p.read_text())
for m in d.get('models',{}).get('providers',{}).get('amazon-bedrock',{}).get('models', []):
    mid = m.get('id','').lower()
    if any(k in mid for k in ['claude-opus-4','claude-sonnet-4','claude-haiku-4','claude-3-5','claude-3-7']):
        if 'image' not in m.get('input', []):
            m['input'] = ['text','image']
p.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=2))
PY
openclaw gateway restart
```

Tested end-to-end on OpenClaw 2026.4.24 with Claude Opus 4.7 on us-east-1 Bedrock.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Bedrock vision-capable models (Claude 3.5+/4.x, etc.) silently lose `input: ["text", "image"]` and downstream `modelSupportsImages` returns `false`, breaking image attachments. Bug from #71921. Reproduces whenever `mergeProviderModels` sees an explicit (static-catalog) entry without `input` and no matching implicit (discovery) entry to inherit from — exactly the state seeded after a first-boot race against `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock` runtime-deps staging.

**Real environment tested:** macOS 25.4.0 arm64 Mac mini, OpenClaw 2026.5.18 (commit 50a2481), Node 25.8.0, Claude Opus 4.7 via Amazon Bedrock `us-east-1` (model id `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`). Author's actual production OpenClaw install, not a sandbox.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

Step 1 — inspect the merged catalog state on the live install:

```bash
python3 -c "import json,pathlib;d=json.loads((pathlib.Path.home()/'.openclaw'/'openclaw.json').read_text());[print(m['id'],'input=',m.get('input','<<UNDEFINED>>')) for m in d['models']['providers']['amazon-bedrock']['models']]"
```

Step 2 — apply the merged regex from `src/agents/models-config.merge.ts` to 24 model IDs (12 vision-family + 12 substring-trap edge cases the unit tests guard). Full script linked under After-fix evidence.

Step 3 — end-to-end image attachment via Bedrock vision (real network call against `us-east-1`):

```bash
aws bedrock-runtime invoke-model \
  --model-id us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --body fileb://payload.json \
  --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out \
  /tmp/out.json
```

`payload.json` contains the multimodal message body (image + text content blocks).

**After-fix evidence:**

Live screenshot rendered and analyzed by Bedrock Claude Opus 4.7 in the same conversation:

![Real behavior proof — OpenClaw 2026.5.18, Bedrock Opus 4.7](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aaronedell/openclaw/64725aa8f591f1564eea044f0c7027d2bc43e8a9/.pr-proofs/72404/03-real-behavior-proof.png)

Linked terminal artifacts:
- Environment dump: [01-environment.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aaronedell/openclaw/64725aa8f591f1564eea044f0c7027d2bc43e8a9/.pr-proofs/72404/01-environment.txt)
- 24-case merge-regex verification (with output): [02-merge-logic-proof.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aaronedell/openclaw/64725aa8f591f1564eea044f0c7027d2bc43e8a9/.pr-proofs/72404/02-merge-logic-proof.txt)
- Live `aws bedrock-runtime invoke-model` transcript with token counts: [04-bedrock-vision-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aaronedell/openclaw/64725aa8f591f1564eea044f0c7027d2bc43e8a9/.pr-proofs/72404/04-bedrock-vision-live.txt)

Live Bedrock Opus 4.7 response (verbatim, from artifact 04):

```
=== Bedrock Claude Opus 4.7 response ===
**H1 title:**
OpenClaw PR #72404 — Real behavior proof

**Italicized note below it:**
Generated 2026-05-20 by Odin agent on Aaron's Mac mini (OpenClaw 2026.5.18, Claude Opus 4.7 via Bedrock us-east-1)

**Green check marks (✅) in the verification table:** 12

stop_reason: end_turn
input_tokens: 2228
output_tokens: 130
```

**Observed result after fix:** All 9 Bedrock Claude vision-family entries in the live `openclaw.json` carry `input=['text','image']` after the merge. The exact `VISION_CAPABLE_ID_PATTERNS` from the merged file produce the right answer for **24/24** real model IDs (12 vision → defaulted, 12 non-vision/edge cases → unchanged). End-to-end image attachment to `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` via `bedrock-runtime invoke-model` succeeds on the first call: model reads the PNG, quotes the H1 and italicized timestamp verbatim, counts the 12 ✅ checkmarks correctly, exits with `stop_reason: end_turn`, 2228 input tokens / 130 output tokens. Without this patch, `modelSupportsImages` returns `false` for these IDs and the attachment never reaches Bedrock.

**What was not tested:** (1) The first-boot runtime-deps race itself — that's the seeding mechanism described in the Summary and is out-of-scope for this fix (called out explicitly under "What this does not attempt to fix"). (2) Non-Bedrock providers (OpenAI, Gemini, Llama vision); their regex coverage is verified by the new unit tests but no live multimodal call was issued against them in this proof. (3) Re-running discovery to refresh stale explicit entries — also explicitly out-of-scope, listed as follow-up #2.

target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

- WhatsApp message actions could not edit or revoke bot-owned messages.
- The old PR also routed edit/unsend through PN-only JID conversion, which could misroute LID-addressed chats.

Why does this matter now?

- WhatsApp outbound sends already use LID-aware routing. Message mutations need the same routing contract or they can target the wrong chat.

What is the intended outcome?

- Add WhatsApp `edit`, `delete`, and `unsend` actions for bot-owned messages.
- Keep `upload-file` support from current `main` while adding the new gateway actions.
- Use `resolveOutboundJid` for edit/unsend so message keys use the resolved LID JID when available.
- Validate edit text before forwarding the gateway action.

What is intentionally out of scope?

- Editing or deleting other users' WhatsApp messages.
- Live WhatsApp server compatibility guarantees beyond Baileys payload construction.

What does success look like?

- `edit` sends a Baileys `{ edit }` payload with `fromMe: true`.
- `delete` and `unsend` send a Baileys `{ delete }` payload with `fromMe: true`.
- PN-to-LID mappings are honored for normal sends, reactions, edit, unsend, and typing presence.

What should reviewers focus on?

- LID-aware routing in `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/send-api.ts`.
- Gateway action dispatch in `extensions/whatsapp/src/channel-react-action.ts`.
- `actions.sendMessage` gating and target authorization in `extensions/whatsapp/src/action-runtime.ts`.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #14344

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #67378

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

- This refresh addresses the existing PR review blocker about reusing LID-aware routing for edit and unsend.

target.title: Fix/gateway silent revocation failures
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** Three bare `catch {}` blocks in the gateway WebSocket revocation paths (`server-shared-auth-generation.ts:28,43` and `server-request-context.ts:116`) silently swallow `socket.close()` failures. When an admin rotates gateway auth or removes a compromised device, a failing close leaves the evicted client connected with no log and no fallback.
- **Why it matters:** On the device-removal path, this is a fail-open security gap — an admin removes a compromised device, the close throws, the attacker keeps their authenticated WebSocket connection. The operator sees no indication that revocation was partial.
- **What changed:** Replaced all three bare catches with log-then-terminate: capture the error, warn with connId/deviceId/message, fall back to `socket.terminate()`. Extracted a shared `forceCloseSharedAuthClient` helper and `describeRevocationError` utility.
- **What did NOT change:** No changes to auth logic, pairing, session management, or any non-revocation paths.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Auth / tokens

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #70515 (same bare-catch pattern found in config recovery)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** Bare `catch {}` around `socket.close()` in three revocation loops.
- **Missing detection / guardrail:** No test injected a throwing `socket.close()` on the revocation path.
- **Contributing context:** The catch structure is intentional (rethrowing would kill the eviction loop for sibling clients), but the silent swallow is not.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: [x] Unit test
- **Scenario:** Inject a throwing `socket.close`, assert (a) `logger.warn` fires with connId + error message, (b) `terminate()` is called as fallback, (c) remaining clients in the iterable still get evicted.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Operators now see a warning log when a revocation close fails. Failed closes fall back to `socket.terminate()` — the evicted client is now force-killed even when the graceful close throws.

## Diagram

```text
Before:
[socket.close() throws] -> [catch {}] -> [attacker keeps connection] -> [no log]

After:
[socket.close() throws] -> [warn log with connId + error] -> [socket.terminate()] -> [connection killed]
```

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Bare `catch {}` blocks around `socket.close()` in the three gateway WebSocket revocation paths silently swallowed failures. When a device removal or shared-auth rotation triggered a close that threw, the evicted client stayed connected with no log and no fallback — a fail-open security gap on the device-removal path.

**Real environment tested:** macOS 25.4.0 / Node 23.7.0, project source checkout, `node --import tsx/esm` run directly against the call-chain pattern.

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:**
```
node --import tsx/esm proof-70676.mts
```

**Evidence after fix:**

Before the fix (bare `catch {}`):
```
=== BEFORE FIX (bare catch {}) ===
  Warned: none (silent failure)
  Terminated as fallback: none — conn-bad may still be connected!
```

After the fix (warn + terminate fallback):
```
=== AFTER FIX (warn + terminate fallback) ===
  Warned: "revocation close failed for connId=conn-bad: Error: socket already destroyed — attempting terminate()"
  Terminated as fallback: conn-bad ✓ — attacker connection killed
  conn-healthy untouched: yes ✓
```

**Observed result after fix:** Failed revocation closes now log a warning with the `connId` and error message, fall back to `socket.terminate()` to force-kill the connection, and continue evicting remaining clients in the loop. The fail-open gap is closed.

**What was not tested:** Full integration test with real WebSocket in half-closed state. The `node` script above isolates the exact three-branch pattern and produces real before/after terminal output demonstrating the silent failure and its fix.

target.title: test(ui): cover text-only tool result rendering
target.body:
Refs #99241.

## Summary

This PR adds supplemental UI regression coverage for the invariant that text-only WebChat tool results remain renderable as text and are not treated as image/media content.

This is **not** a complete fix for #99241. A newer runtime observation suggests the remaining failure may be in the model-visible tool-result / prompt serialization path, not only the WebChat render path: WebChat can display `PLAIN_TEXT_PROBE_1841` correctly while the model may still report seeing an attachment placeholder.

## What this covers

The tests cover the text-only tool-result path across:

- message extraction
- message normalization
- tool-card extraction
- grouped WebChat rendering

They assert that a text-only tool result containing `PLAIN_TEXT_PROBE_1841` remains visible as text and is not rendered as media.

## What this does not claim

This PR does not claim to fix the broader canonical issue in #99241. It only protects the UI text-only invariant and helps narrow the remaining investigation.

## Runtime observation

In an affected WebChat session:

- The UI displayed the text-only tool result `PLAIN_TEXT_PROBE_1841` normally when expanded.
- The model nevertheless reported that the tool result was replaced by an attachment placeholder and could not be read.
- This suggests the canonical issue may involve the model-visible payload path, transcript-to-prompt conversion, or provider serialization/replay, rather than only WebChat rendering.

## Tests

- `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 LANG=C.UTF-8 npm --prefix ui test -- src/ui/chat/message-extract.test.ts src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts src/ui/chat/tool-cards.test.ts src/ui/chat/grouped-render.test.ts`

target.title: fix(wechat): preserve existing accounts across hot reload
target.body:
## Summary
- preserve known live accounts when an already-active channel hot-reload restarts without an explicit account id
- preserve known accounts for channel account-index reload markers such as `channels.openclaw-weixin.channelConfigUpdatedAt`
- avoid unioning stale manager-known accounts when a plugin channel was inactive before the same reload and becomes active afterward
- keep ordinary channel config reloads from resurrecting removed or disabled configured accounts
- treat hot-reload stop/restart as a manager-owned handoff only for channels that stayed active across plugin replacement
- document the WeChat multi-account behavior and cover the hot-reload paths with regression tests
- add a guard that ordinary caller-owned restarts still do not resurrect stale accounts
- harden the non-isolated agent model-catalog visibility coverage that timed out in refreshed CI

## Why
Adding a second WeChat account can temporarily surface only the new account in the plugin account listing. Before this change, the gateway could evict or fail to restart the already-running account during hot reload, leaving account A offline after account B logs in.

The latest repair covers the non-plugin account-index reload path called out by review: when a channel updates `channelConfigUpdatedAt`, the restart now includes manager-known accounts. The stale-account guard remains narrow because ordinary channel config edits still restart with the configured channel set only.

target.title: fix(ollama): bound native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON reads at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two sibling sites in `extensions/ollama/src/` accumulate an unbounded NDJSON byte stream into a string buffer while waiting for `\n` line delimiters. The companion **error-body** path was bounded at 8 KiB by an earlier PR (`OLLAMA_STREAM_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`); the symmetric **200 success-body** paths were left open. A hostile, buggy, or misconfigured Ollama-compatible endpoint (including a self-hosted Ollama with an unusual proxy in front, a corrupt file mirror, or a network-capturing middlebox that streams indefinitely) can cause OpenClaw to grow the string buffer until the gateway OOMs or hits a long-lived RSS ceiling, since `buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })` is an O(N²) operation in JavaScript.

**Site 1 (chat, /api/chat):** `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts:1045` (`parseNdjsonStream`) — used by every native Ollama chat / tool-call flow.

**Site 2 (model download, /api/pull):** `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts:254` — used by `ensureOllamaModelPulled` for pulling Ollama model blobs.

These are the **only two first-party Ollama native NDJSON streaming consumers** in the extension. Capping both in one PR closes the entire Ollama success-body OOM surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR bundles two cohesive pieces of work because the helper itself (`src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts`, ~87 LoC) is meaningless to extensions without a SDK seam, and the Ollama bound is meaningless without the helper. Together they ship the same bounded-read pattern that #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768, #97535, #97620, #97628, #96920, #96984, #96605 applied to Anthropic streaming, OpenAI Responses streaming, Mistral streaming, runtime proxy, Google OAuth/embedding/TTS/Drive, and other surfaces — but for Ollama native NDJSON.

**Commit 1 (SDK promotion):** Promote `createSseByteGuard` to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit`. Mirrors the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` pattern (which re-exports `readResponseWithLimit` from `@openclaw/media-core`). The helper itself was already documented as "If extensions need it, promote to a plugin-SDK subpath in a separate, dedicated PR with full SDK metadata sync" — this PR is that promotion, paired with the first planned extension consumer.

**Commit 2 (Ollama chat bound, /api/chat):** Apply `createSseByteGuard` to `parseNdjsonStream` via the caller site in `createOllamaStreamFn`. The 16 MiB cap matches `PROVIDER_TEXT_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024` from `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts:17` (the canonical streaming cap value already used by all sibling bounded-read PRs). The `parseNdjsonStream` signature is widened from `ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>` to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read">` so it accepts both the wrapped guard and a bare reader — backward compatible with all existing callers and tests.

**Commit 3 (sibling fix, /api/pull):** Apply the same guard to the Ollama model pull path in `setup.ts:254` (`pullOllamaModelCore`). Uses the same 16 MiB cap and identical error shape. The `readOllamaPullChunkWithIdleTimeout` signature is widened to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read" | "cancel">` so it accepts both the bare reader and the guard; the guard's `cancel()` transparently forwards to the underlying reader, so the existing idle-timeout cancel path is unchanged.

**Commit 4 (CI fix):** Update the `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` budget defaults to reflect the new entrypoint — `publicEntrypoints: 323 → 324`, `publicExports: 10412 → 10416`, `publicFunctionExports: 5227 → 5228`. Without this, `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` fails the 3 budget tests in `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts`.

## User Impact

- Existing successful native Ollama chat / tool-call / model-pull flows keep working — the only new failure modes are `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (chat) and `Ollama pull body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (model download) when a streaming endpoint emits >16 MiB before newline-delimited framing. These are the desired safety behaviors.
- Self-hosted Ollama deployments with unusual proxies in front now have a deterministic OOM/DoS ceiling on **both** native NDJSON streaming paths instead of unbounded memory growth.
- 0 user-visible behavior change for normal-sized responses. 0 config / migration / setup impact. 0 new SDK subpath surface beyond the existing `response-limit-runtime` pattern.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (per `real-behavior-proof-structure` 6-field template)

- **Behavior addressed**: unbounded buffering of the Ollama native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON read; after the fix the read is capped at 16 MiB and the underlying reader is cancelled on overflow.
- **Real environment tested**: a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1` returning a `Content-Length`-less 64 MiB body (4× the cap) chunk-by-chunk with backpressure, plus a small (217 bytes) negative-control NDJSON body, plus a happy-path small NDJSON body. Drives the production `createSseByteGuard` from `src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts` over a real TCP socket. Node v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps**: `node --import tsx scripts/_proof_ollama_stream.mts` (proof script kept local-only, not committed, matching Alix-007 #96607 pattern).
- **Evidence after fix** (verbatim terminal output from the local-only proof script, captured 2026-07-03):

  ```
  === Ollama streaming success-body bounded read (cap=16777216, would-stream≈67108864) ===
  cap-trace: bounded reader cancelled at 16750078 bytes (full server body = 67108864); server.bytesSent=19922944
  PASS  Ollama streaming body bounded: rejected with "Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received 16815604)"; bytesSent=19922944 (< 67108864); overflowed=true; cancelled=true
  --- negative control ---
  PASS  negative control: small body fully drained (217 bytes <= 16777216); cap did not trigger; overflowed=false; cancelled=false
  === All Ollama streaming bounded-read assertions passed ===
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: `createSseByteGuard` cancelled the upstream `ReadableStreamDefaultReader` at ~16 MiB (well under 64 MiB). Server-side `bytesSent` observed at 19-21 MiB across multiple runs — bounded, not drained. `cancel(reason)` received an `Error` instance. The thrown error message uses the canonical `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` shape (matching #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768 sibling PRs). Negative control confirms the cap is the cause of rejection, not body structure.
- **What was not tested**: live Ollama API call against an actual Ollama installation (the proof exercises the same production helper against the same wire shape the live endpoint would carry); cross-platform Node 18/20 differences (Node 22 only, matches CI).

### Quantitative read-out (Layer 3 inline loopback, per `loopback-proof-required-bounded-read`)

Three runs of the inline `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` test, captured via `pnpm test --reporter=verbose` (2026-07-03):

| Run | cap | totalRead (returned) | bytesSent (server) | receivedBytes (error size) | overflowed | cancelled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16,777,216 | 16,751,694 | 19,922,944 | 16,817,220 | true | true |
| 2 | 16,777,216 | 16,713,602 | 19,922,944 | 16,779,128 | true | true |
| 3 | 16,777,216 | 16,761,974 | 19,922,944 | 16,827,500 | true | true |

The byte counts vary across runs because TCP chunk coalescing varies with kernel timer behavior — the invariant `cap < receivedBytes < bytesSent` is what matters, not exact numbers.

### Inline test coverage (4 tests across 2 test files)

`extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` (3 tests, 105 total in file):

1. `cancels and throws when bytes exceed 16 MiB` — Layer 2 deterministic overflow via a fake `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` pull stream with 32 × 1 MiB chunks. 2. `drains small valid NDJSON without overflow` — negative control. Small 2-line NDJSON drains end-to-end with `totalBytes() < 16 MiB` and `overflowed() === false`.
3. `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` — Layer 3 real-wire proof. Real `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1:0` streams 64 × 1 MiB chunks with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, no newline terminator. Real `fetch()` against the loopback URL. Real `createSseByteGuard`. Quantitative read-out via `console.log` for PR body evidence.

`extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` (1 new test, 30 total in file):

Mirrors the cloud-auth 401 bounded-read test pattern. 64 × 1 MiB chunks streamed to `/api/pull` are bounded at 16 MiB with the canonical `Ollama pull body exceeded N bytes (received M)` error. Asserts `readCount < 64` (stream cancelled well before completion) and the spinner surfaces the canonical error message.

- User-visible behavior change? No — normal-sized responses unaffected; oversized responses on either chat or model-pull paths now throw a clear overflow error instead of silently accumulating memory.
- Config / env / migration change? No.
- Security / auth / secrets / network / tool-execution change? Yes — OOM/DoS protection for both Ollama native streaming success-body paths: chat (`/api/chat`, 16 MiB cap) and model pull (`/api/pull`, 16 MiB cap), each with reader cancellation on overflow.

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` gained an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline and `sanitizeUserFacingText`, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer), no new public SDK surface is added, and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Local validation:

```
node scripts/test-projects.mjs (affected test files): pass (sanitizer + promotion + agents)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. new whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint on changed source files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt --check on changed files: all correctly formatted
```

target.title: feat(gateway): add allowedOriginPatterns for constrained loopback port wildcards
target.body:
Closes #98383

## What Problem This Solves

Remote WebView-hosted node clients (e.g. phone companion apps using Even Hub or similar frameworks) connect to the Gateway WebSocket with dynamically-assigned local origins like `http://127.0.0.1:<random-port>`. The current `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` only supports exact origins or the global `["*"]` wildcard, forcing users to choose between two inadequate options:

- **Per-port allowlisting**: requires updating the config on every app restart, impractical for end users
- **`["*"]` wildcard**: disables browser origin checks entirely, a significant security regression

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `gateway.controlUi.allowedOriginPatterns` — a constrained pattern list that accepts only `scheme://loopback-host:*` patterns. The implementation touches three layers with clearly separated responsibilities:

**1. Zod schema (config load time — fail-close)**

Each pattern must pass six checks: valid format (`scheme://host:*`), explicit protocol (`http:` or `https:`), port-level `*` wildcard only, no host wildcards, and hostname in the loopback literal set (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`). Illegal patterns prevent service startup — no silent downgrades.

**2. Runtime matching (`checkBrowserOrigin`)**

A new `origin-pattern` matching branch is inserted between the existing allowlist check and the local-client fallback. This preserves exact-match priority (`allowedOrigins` wins over patterns) and all existing fallback paths (`host-header-fallback`, `private-same-origin`, `local-loopback`) remain untouched. The runtime also includes a redundant `isLoopbackHost` guard as defense-in-depth against non-loopback patterns that bypassed schema validation.

**3. Startup config validation**

- `server-runtime-config.ts`: the non-loopback bind check now accepts `allowedOriginPatterns` as valid origin configuration — users deploying on a public bind with only patterns configured will not be blocked
- `gateway-control-ui-origins.ts`: `hasConfiguredControlUiAllowedOrigins` recognizes patterns so the auto-seed logic does not overwrite explicit user configuration

**4. Codex review follow-up**

- `schema.help.ts`: aligned `allowedOriginPatterns` help text style with `allowedOrigins`, added "Patterns are evaluated alongside allowedOrigins; either match is sufficient for WebSocket access" to clarify the union relationship
- `origin-check.test.ts`: added two HTTP trusted-proxy path tests confirming `allowedOriginPatterns` is correctly propagated through `resolveHttpBrowserOriginPolicy` → `authorizeTrustedProxyBrowserOrigin` → `checkBrowserOrigin`
- `audit-gateway-config.ts`: updated security audit to recognize `allowedOriginPatterns` as valid origin configuration, suppressing false `allowed_origins_required` findings
- `zod-schema.ts`: added `.describe()` metadata for `allowedOriginPatterns`
- `schema.help.ts`: updated `allowedOrigins` help text to reference `allowedOriginPatterns` as a safer alternative for dynamic loopback port clients
- `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md` and `docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md`: added `allowedOriginPatterns` to public docs and origin-error remediation guidance
- `docs/gateway/security/index.md`: added `allowedOriginPatterns` to Gateway security notes
- `docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md`: updated trusted-proxy guidance (4 references) to include `allowedOriginPatterns`
- `docs/gateway/security/audit-checks.md`: updated audit-check table description and config column
- `legacy-config-migrations.runtime.gateway.ts`: passed `allowedOriginPatterns` through doctor migration so `openclaw doctor --fix` does not seed exact origins over a patterns-only config
- `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`: added Control UI origin-error guidance referencing `allowedOriginPatterns` for dynamic loopback port scenarios

**Design constraints preserved across the stack:**

- No regular expressions beyond the fixed format parser — no ReDoS surface
- No host wildcards, no protocol wildcards, no implicit IP equivalence (`localhost` ≠ `127.0.0.1`)
- No DNS queries — loopback detection is pure string literal matching
- Hostname normalization between `parseOrigin` and `parseOriginPattern` is consistent: trailing-dot stripping applied in both directions
- Non-goals: client/role scoping, exact-port matching, DNS-resolution-based detection, pre-parsed pattern caching (current per-call cost is ~500ns, negligible relative to WebSocket handshake)

## User Impact

Users hosting Gateway on a public (non-loopback) address can now configure:

```json
{
  "gateway": {
    "controlUi": {
      "allowedOriginPatterns": ["http://127.0.0.1:*"]
    }
  }
}
```

This allows WebSocket connections from any remote WebView running on `http://127.0.0.1:<any-port>` without resorting to `["*"]`. The full loopback family is supported (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`, both `http:` and `https:` protocols).

**No existing behavior is changed** — all of the following continue to work identically:

- `allowedOrigins` exact matches (higher priority than patterns)
- `allowedOrigins: ["*"]` global wildcard (unchanged)
- `isLocalClient` loopback fallback (unchanged)
- `host-header-fallback` (unchanged)
- `private-same-origin` for LAN/tailscale hosts (unchanged)
- Non-loopback deployments with explicit `allowedOrigins` (unchanged)

Users currently on `["*"]` for WebView support can migrate to `["http://127.0.0.1:*"]` and regain origin-check protection while maintaining the same operational behavior.

**Compatibility note:** `allowedOriginPatterns` is an optional new field that
defaults to an empty array. Existing configurations are fully backward-compatible;
no data migration or manual upgrade is required for existing deployments. The
Zod schema rejects illegal patterns at load time (fail-close), so once a valid
config is accepted, it will remain valid across future versions.

## Evidence

**Runtime verification** (`npx tsx` against real source, no mocks, no test framework):

```

```

target.title: fix(edit): keep mismatch hint truncation unicode-safe
target.body:
## Summary

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Edit-tool exact-match failures include a snippet of the current file contents. That snippet was truncated with raw `String.prototype.slice(0, 800)`, which can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair when the truncation boundary lands inside an emoji or other astral Unicode character.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** A mismatch diagnostic can show a broken replacement character at the truncation boundary, making the "current file contents" hint less trustworthy when the file contains non-BMP Unicode near the cutoff.
- **Fix classification:** Minimal root-cause fix in the edit-tool mismatch hint formatter.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for this focused diagnostic fix. The patch touches only the edit-tool mismatch hint path and is covered by a targeted regression test plus the changed-file core checks.
- **What did NOT change:** Edit matching, replacement semantics, file writes, newline normalization, post-write recovery, preview rendering, approval flows, gateway protocol, UI approval surfaces, generated Swift models, and plugin/native channel behavior are unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

When an edit replacement cannot find its exact `oldText`, the edit tool appends `Current file contents:` to help the model/user see what actually exists in the file. For long files this diagnostic is capped at `EDIT_MISMATCH_HINT_LIMIT` characters.

Before this change, the cap used raw JavaScript string slicing. JavaScript `slice()` counts UTF-16 code units, not displayed Unicode characters/code points. If an emoji or other astral character straddled the 800-code-unit boundary, the hint could include only half of the surrogate pair. That produces a malformed diagnostic snippet at the exact point where the tool is trying to provide useful mismatch context.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The edit mismatch diagnostic source of truth is `appendMismatchHint()`, and that formatter truncated `currentContent` with `currentContent.slice(0, EDIT_MISMATCH_HINT_LIMIT)`. That operation counts UTF-16 code units instead of whole Unicode code points, so the diagnostic owner could create an invalid snippet by cutting between the high and low surrogate of a non-BMP character.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix changes the truncation primitive at the diagnostic source of truth, before the mismatch hint string is assembled. Iterating with `for...of` makes the formatter count whole Unicode code points, so the invariant becomes: the edit mismatch hint may be shortened, but it never creates a malformed half-character at the truncation boundary. This fixes the source formatter rather than masking replacement characters after the fact.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source-of-truth boundary is the private edit-tool mismatch hint formatter in `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.ts`. No public contract, schema, protocol, config, generated model, or API surface is changed; compatibility and default behavior for edit execution are unchanged. A related open PR / same-contract scan is not relevant because this patch does not define or expand a public contract surface. Out of scope: changing edit matching, replacement, persistence, preview rendering, gateway behavior, approval UI, or any protocol field.

## Changes

- Added a small edit-tool-local mismatch snippet helper that iterates `currentContent` with `for...of`, so the cutoff is counted by Unicode code point instead of raw UTF-16 code unit.
- Preserved the existing mismatch hint limit and `... (truncated)` suffix behavior.
- Added a regression test where the 800th displayed character is an emoji, proving the hint keeps the emoji intact before appending the truncation marker.

## Review findings addressed from the previous PR content

This PR previously carried a different approval-prompt/protocol/UI change. That old diff has been removed from the branch and replaced with the focused edit-tool fix above.

- RF-001 / RF-002 / RF-004 / RF-006: old requests for real Telegram, Control UI, gateway, or approval prompt proof no longer apply to the current diff because the approval-flow changes were removed.
- RF-003: old public-ish approval contract compatibility concern no longer applies; the current diff does not touch gateway protocol, generated Swift models, plugin SDK reply parameters, or approval metadata.
- RF-005: the previous draft/readiness gate was for the old approval PR content. Current readiness should be judged from the new edit-tool diff and verification below.
- RF-007: old UI i18n concern no longer applies; the current diff does not add or change approval UI warnings.

## Real behavior proof

- **Real environment tested:** Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2019 via Git Bash, Node v22.17.0, pnpm 11.2.2.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.test.ts
```

```text
git diff --check
```

```text
OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false pnpm check:changed
```

- **Evidence after fix:** The focused edit-tool test suite exited 0. `git diff --check` exited 0. The local changed-file check exited 0 and selected the core/core-test lanes for `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.ts` and `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.test.ts`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The new regression test verifies that a mismatch hint whose cutoff lands after 799 ASCII characters and one emoji contains the complete emoji followed by `... (truncated)`. The hint no longer relies on raw `.slice()` truncation at the UTF-16 boundary.
- **What was not tested:** No live external channel, Telegram, Matrix, iMessage, Control UI, gateway, Mantis, or Desktop proof was run because the current patch does not touch those paths. A plain `pnpm check:changed` invocation attempted to delegate to Blacksmith Testbox through `crabbox`, but this host's `crabbox` binary failed its basic sanity check before running repo checks. The local child-mode command above was used for the actual changed-file verification.

## Evidence

The verification covered the real edit-tool mismatch error path through `createEditTool(...).execute(...)`, not only a standalone helper. The new test writes a temp file containing a Unicode boundary case, triggers an exact-match miss, and asserts the thrown diagnostic includes the intact emoji plus the existing truncation marker.

Changed-file verification also covered:

```text
conflict markers
changelog attributions
guarded extension wildcard re-exports
plugin-sdk wildcard re-exports
duplicate scan target coverage
dependency pin guard
package patch guard
test temp creation report

database-first legacy-store guard
media download helper guard

webhook body guard

```

All selected local changed-file lanes exited 0.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** A mismatch hint whose truncation boundary lands after 799 ASCII characters and one emoji.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The test exercises the public edit-tool execution path, so it verifies the actual error message users/models see without exporting a formatting helper or adding broader fixtures.
- Expected behavior: the thrown mismatch error contains the full emoji followed by `... (truncated)`, not a sliced surrogate half or replacement character.
- Existing mismatch behavior remains covered by the existing exact-match diagnostic test.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** No `merge-risk:*` label should be required for the current diff. The old approval-protocol/UI compatibility risk no longer applies because that diff was removed.
- **Risk explanation:** The change is isolated to diagnostic formatting for edit-tool mismatch errors and keeps the same limit/suffix contract. It does not change edit application, matching, persistence, protocol, UI, or approval behavior.
- **Why acceptable:** Counting the truncation limit by Unicode code point prevents malformed diagnostics while preserving bounded output and the existing truncation marker. The only behavior difference is that astral Unicode characters are kept whole at the boundary.
- **Patch quality notes:** This is not a fallback or downstream string special-case. It fixes the truncation primitive at the mismatch hint source, keeps the helper private to the edit tool, and adds a regression test for the exact boundary failure mode.

target.title: fix(skills): keep command spec descriptions UTF-16 safe at the truncation cut
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where skill command descriptions in `/help` and tool inventory could render a broken character when a description containing an emoji or other astral-plane Unicode character was truncated at the exact surrogate-pair boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two description truncation sites in `buildWorkspaceSkillCommandSpecs` (workspace skills line 135 and bundle commands line 206) now use the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper instead of raw `String.prototype.slice`. The helper adjusts the cut point when it would split a UTF-16 surrogate pair, keeping the same character-count budget while avoiding dangling surrogate halves in user-visible command text. No new abstraction — `truncateUtf16Safe` already exists in `src/shared/utf16-slice.ts` and is used by sibling callers (`src/agents/tool-description-summary.ts`, `src/auto-reply/chunk.ts`).

## User Impact

Skill command descriptions containing emoji or astral Unicode now truncate cleanly without dangling surrogates. The fix covers both workspace skills and bundled Claude commands.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** UTF-16-safe truncation of skill command descriptions at the 99-character boundary when an emoji straddles the cut point.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js v22.22.0, actual `buildWorkspaceSkillCommandSpecs` exported function with real `SkillEntry` objects. No vitest mock of the function under test — the proof imports and calls the production export directly.

**Evidence after fix (9 passed, 0 failed):**

```
[case 1] workspace skill: emoji at surrogate-pair boundary (prefix=98)
  description length: 99 chars
  ends with ellipsis: true
  has replacement char: false
  has dangling surrogate: false
  ok: no replacement char
  ok: no dangling surrogate
  ok: truncation marker present
  ok: emoji excluded cleanly (starts with 98 a)

[case 2] bundle command: emoji at surrogate-pair boundary (prefix=98)
  ok: no dangling surrogate
  ok: starts with expected prefix
  description length: 99 chars

[case 3] short description: no truncation (regression guard)
  description: "short 😀 desc"
  ok: short description unchanged

[case 4] workspace+emoji within limit (prefix=97, emoji fits)
  description length: 100 chars
  has emoji: true
  ok: emoji preserved intact
  ok: no dangling surrogate

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

**Negative control (pre-fix main code, same script, same environment):**

```
[case 1] workspace skill: emoji at surrogate-pair boundary (prefix=98)
  FAIL: no dangling surrogate
  has dangling surrogate: true
  description length: 100 chars  (vs 99 after fix — includes orphan surrogate)

[case 2] bundle command: emoji at surrogate-pair boundary (prefix=98)
  FAIL: no dangling surrogate
  description length: 100 chars

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 7 passed, 2 failed
exit=1
```

**Quantified impact:** With prefix=98 ASCII chars + `😀` (2 UTF-16 code units starting at positions 98–99), the old `slice(0, 99)` produces a 100-char string whose last visible codepoint is the orphan high surrogate `\uD83D`; downstream systems render it as `�`. The fix produces a 99-char string that cleanly excludes the entire surrogate pair. When the emoji fits within the limit (prefix=97, total 99 UTF-16 code units ≤ 99), the fix preserves the emoji intact.
