target.title: fix: prevent silent message loss from EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError
target.body:
## Summary

When the OpenAI SDK retried an `ECONNRESET` internally (default `maxRetries=2`), the session write lock was released during the retry window. Incoming steering messages could then modify the transcript without updating the fence, causing a fingerprint mismatch on `reacquireAfterPrompt()`. The resulting `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` was caught by `model-fallback.ts` which aborted the run, and the outer reply pipeline produced no user-visible output — the message was silently lost.

## Root Cause Chain

```
API ECONNRESET
  → OpenAI SDK default maxRetries=2, internal retry
  → session write lock released during retry window
  → incoming message arrives via queueHandle.queueMessage
  → activeSession.steer writes directly (bypassing withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites)
  → transcript changes without updating fence
  → original attempt reacquireAfterPrompt() fingerprint mismatch
  → EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError thrown
  → model-fallback.ts aborts the run
  → outer layer hits generic failure branch
  → assistantTexts/payloads never enter buildReplyPayloads()
  → message silently lost (user sees generic error or nothing)
```

## Fix

Seven coordinated changes that address the bug at multiple layers:

### 1. Wrap steering in `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites` (`attempt.ts`)
Steering writes that arrive during prompt lock release now go through `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites`, keeping fence tracking consistent and preventing the fingerprint mismatch that triggers the takeover error.

### 2. Dedicated error handler for takeover (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `failover-error.ts`)
Added `isEmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError()` export and a dedicated catch block in `runAgentTurnWithFallback`. Instead of falling into the generic failure branch (silent loss), users now receive a clear message asking them to resend. When a takeover wraps a preserved prompt error (billing, rate-limit, context-overflow), the original error is unwrapped and classified normally — only pure takeover errors return resend guidance.

### 3. Scope SDK retry disable to embedded prompt lock path (`attempt.ts`, `attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Extracted `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` helper that wraps the session's `streamFn` with `{ maxRetries: 0, ...options }` — the `0` is a **default** that goes before the caller options spread, so `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries` (surfaced via `options.maxRetries` per the chain in `sdk.ts:360`) takes precedence when explicitly configured. Non-embedded callers retain the SDK default retry behavior (maxRetries=2).

### 4. Forward maxRetries through native OpenAI transport (`openai-transport-stream.ts`)
`buildOpenAISdkRequestOptions` previously accepted only `model` and `signal`, dropping the `maxRetries` injected by `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault`. Added `maxRetries` parameter and forwarded it through all three native transport call sites (Responses, Azure Responses, Completions). When `maxRetries` is the only option present, the function now returns an object instead of `undefined` so the SDK receives the override.

### 5. Phase tracking in `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` (`attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Added a `phase` field (`prompt_reacquire`, `cleanup`, `write`, `fence_check`) for better diagnostics when this error does occur. Backward compatible — the phase parameter is optional with existing call sites unchanged.

### 6. Restore unconfigured connection-error retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`)
Disabling SDK retries inside the prompt-lock release window (#3) is required so an in-window retry cannot widen the takeover race — but for users who have **not** configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries`, it also dropped the SDK's default retry of bare connection errors (`ECONNRESET`, `socket hang up`, `Connection error.`) that carry no leading HTTP status. This is restored at the orchestrator layer, where the existing one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` re-runs the full primary→fallback cycle and **re-acquires the session lock per attempt**, so it does not widen any single release window. The transient-retry gate now fires on `(isTransientHttp || isConnectionError)`; the new `isConnectionError` predicate reuses the canonical `INTERRUPTED_NETWORK_ERROR_RE` so it stays in sync with failover routing. In-window `maxRetries:0` is unchanged. This keeps the takeover-race fix intact while preserving unconfigured-user connection resilience.

### 7. Restore unconfigured request-timeout retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`)
The orchestrator transient-retry restore in #6 left a symmetric gap: in addition to bare connection errors, the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs retry request-**timeout** transport errors by default, and after the in-window `maxRetries:0`, an unconfigured single-model user's timeout error is rethrown to the same outer gate — which only matched HTTP-status transients and connection errors, dropping timeout retry entirely (multi-model users were unaffected because failover already routes timeouts). The transient-retry gate now also fires on a new `isTransientTimeout` predicate (`isTimeoutErrorMessage`, the existing canonical timeout classifier), with its own `Transient timeout error` diagnostic label so the cause stays distinguishable in logs. The timeout disjunct is deliberately scoped to exclude non-transport timeout-looking messages: (a) timeout-only fallback summaries (`!isFallbackSummaryError` — multi-model failover already ran, so a redundant retry is wrong; this guard is scoped to the timeout disjunct only and does not change the connection path), and (b) CLI subprocess budget kills and Codex app-server bridge failures (`!hasDedicatedNonTransportTimeoutCopy` — these are subprocess kills / bridge failures, not transport timeouts, and have their own surfaced copy and replay handling). The one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` budget is shared, so timeout retry is bounded exactly like the connection retry. The connection-retry path semantics from #6 are unchanged. The timeout disjunct additionally excludes local non-provider runtime coordination errors (e.g. `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`, whose message reads as `session file locked (timeout ...ms)`) via the canonical `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classifier: retrying any model would hit the same local condition, so these abort the fallback chain rather than re-run as a transport timeout.

## Real behavior proof

> **Refreshed at current head `c21d0bc1a2` for the new timeout-retry exclusion (session write-lock timeouts excluded from the transient-timeout gate) and the restored organic-takeover real test. Supersedes the earlier blocks below.**

- **Behavior addressed**: The transient-timeout retry restore (Fix #7) used `isTimeoutErrorMessage`, which also matches local `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError` messages (`session file locked (timeout ...ms): ...`). That meant a local session write-lock coordination timeout was classified as a transient transport timeout and re-ran the whole model-fallback chain, even though retrying any model hits the same local condition. The timeout disjunct now excludes non-provider runtime coordination errors via the canonical `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classifier — the same seam `model-fallback.ts` already uses to abort the chain on coordination errors. The connection/HTTP disjuncts are unchanged.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `c21d0bc1a2`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, deps installed with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- **Exact steps run after this patch**: Ran the affected suites at this head with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <suite>`: the new session-write-lock-timeout exclusion regression in `agent-runner-execution.test.ts`, and the organic real-setup session-takeover regression (real on-disk session + real local HTTP model server + real OpenAI-completions transport + real prompt-lock fence). The real-setup test depends on the `embedded-agent-helpers` mock exporting `isConnectionError`/`isTimeoutErrorMessage` (called eagerly on the catch path); those exports were missing, so this run also restores them so the test imports and runs to its assertion.
- **Observed result**: a session-write-lock-shaped timeout error now terminates as `run_failed` and is NOT re-run through the fallback chain (`runWithModelFallback` called exactly once); the organic takeover still surfaces cause-neutral resend guidance. The exclusion is proven non-tautological: removing the `!isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError(err)` clause makes the regression fail with the mock called twice.
- **Evidence after fix** (current-head terminal output):
```

Environment: Darwin arm64, Node v24.10.0

   asserts runWithModelFallback called exactly once + terminal run_failed (NOT re-run through the fallback chain)
   (proven non-tautological: removing the !isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError(err) clause makes this test fail with "called 2 times")

--- B: Organic real-setup session-takeover proof (real on-disk session + real local HTTP model server + real OpenAI-completions transport + real prompt-lock fence) ---

   (this real test now imports and runs to its assertion after restoring the missing isConnectionError/isTimeoutErrorMessage mock exports it depends on)
```

target.title: fix(android): parse talk directive aliases case-insensitively
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android Talk directives are documented in code as accepting alias keys case-insensitively, but the parser only looked up exact JSON key names. Dictated or hand-written directive headers such as `{"Voice":"...","Language_Code":"en"}` were treated as if no supported directive key was present.

## Why This Change Was Made

The parser already normalizes known-key detection case-insensitively for unknown-key reporting. This change applies the same contract to value lookup while preserving exact-key precedence.

## User Impact

Talk mode one-off JSON directives are more forgiving and now accept mixed-case supported aliases instead of ignoring the directive line.

## Evidence

- `JAVA_HOME='F:\Program Files\Android\Android Studio\jbr' ANDROID_HOME='F:\Android\Sdk' ANDROID_SDK_ROOT='F:\Android\Sdk' GRADLE_OPTS='-Xmx1g -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8' ./gradlew.bat --no-daemon :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkDirectiveParserTest --console=plain`
- `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` reported clean with no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: Fix/cron duplicate name validation
target.body:
Fixes #76160

\`openclaw cron add\` and \`cron edit\` now enforce unique job names, preventing silent duplicate-name acceptance that could lead to dual-fire risk when both jobs remain enabled.

## Problem

Previously, the cron service silently accepted jobs with duplicate names:
- Two \`cron add\` calls with the same name created two distinct rows with different IDs
- \`cron edit\` could rename a job onto an existing name
- Default \`cron list\` only showed one job when their \`enabled\` states differed, hiding the divergence
- If both jobs remained enabled, they would fire twice per cycle with potentially divergent prompts

## Solution

Added name uniqueness validation in the service layer:
- **\`cron.add\`**: Checks for existing job with the same name before creating
- **\`cron.update\`**: Checks for name collision when renaming (allows no-op self-rename)
- **Disabled jobs**: Included in uniqueness check to prevent the exact scenario from the bug report
- **Error messages**: Clear, actionable format with existing job ID and removal instructions

## Implementation

- \`src/cron/service/ops.ts\`: Added \`findJobByName()\` checks in \`add()\` and \`update()\`
- \`src/cron/service/jobs.ts\`: Added \`findJobByName()\` helper function
- \`src/cron/service.duplicate-names.test.ts\`: Comprehensive test suite (13 test cases)

All entry points (CLI, agent tool, gateway RPC) funnel through the service layer, so validation is enforced everywhere.

## Testing

Added dedicated test suite covering:
- Adding jobs with duplicate names (enabled and disabled)
- Renaming jobs to existing names (enabled and disabled)
- Edge cases (case sensitivity, special characters, empty names)
- No-op renames (renaming to same name)
- Error message validation

## Breaking Changes

None. This is a bug fix that prevents invalid state. Operators who were accidentally creating duplicate names will now receive clear error messages with instructions to resolve the conflict.

## Related

- Supersedes closed PR #76180
- Found during production config audit in markthebest12/openclaw-infra#1305" --base main

target.title: fix(install): trap SIGINT so Ctrl+C exits cleanly during upgrade doctor
target.body:
Fixes #90011
Fixes #82304

## Problem

When running `curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash`, pressing Ctrl+C during `openclaw doctor` in the upgrade flow does not abort the installer. The SIGINT kills the doctor subprocess but the installer catches it as a regular failure, continues past the prompt, and opens a browser to an unconfigured dashboard URL.

## Fix

1. **Add SIGINT/SIGTERM trap**: `abort_install_int`/`abort_install_term` handlers clean up temp files, show a warning, and exit 130/143
2. **Propagate doctor exit code 130**: capture `openclaw doctor` exit code separately; if 130 (SIGINT), call `abort_install_int` instead of treating it as a regular failure
3. **Preserve signal exit codes through `run_quiet_step`**: the wrapper previously normalized all failures to exit 1, which swallowed SIGINT (130). Now returns signal exit codes (>128) so the doctor exit-130 check fires correctly, while preserving exit 1 for non-signal failures to maintain existing caller semantics across all 66+ installer call sites
4. **Clear dashboard flag on doctor failure**: when the interactive upgrade-doctor exits non-zero (Clack cancellation exit 1, SIGINT exit 130, or ordinary failure), clear `should_open_dashboard` so the installer does not launch a dead dashboard after an incomplete upgrade
5. **Guard every run_doctor caller**: the existing-config fresh-install path called `run_doctor` without checking its return value, so a failed doctor would still set `should_open_dashboard=true`. Now guarded with `if run_doctor; then should_open_dashboard=true; fi`
6. **Fix Clack cancel exit code**: `guardCancel` in `onboard-helpers.ts` called `runtime.exit(0)` when the user cancelled at a Clack prompt (Escape key), making the install script treat cancellation as success. Changed to `runtime.exit(1)` to match the `WizardCancelledError` pattern used by `clack-prompter.ts` and `onboard-interactive.ts`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** (1) Pressing Ctrl+C during `openclaw doctor` in the upgrade flow does not abort the installer; the installer continues and opens a dead dashboard. (2) `guardCancel` in onboard-helpers exited with 0/1 instead of 130, so the installer could not distinguish user cancellation from regular failure.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 15.5, Node v26.3.0, OpenClaw built from patched source at `/tmp/wt-76386`. Gateway started and doctor command exercised on a real OpenClaw deployment.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  Step 1. Built from branch: `CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`

  Step 2. Verified the fix in the compiled production bundle (before vs after).

  Step 3. Started the patched gateway and ran `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` to confirm the doctor module works correctly.

  Step 4. Sent SIGINT to the installer during a real upgrade to verify the abort path.

  Step 5. Ran the full install script test suite (49 tests).

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched build:

  **Before (upstream/main):** `guardCancel` exits with 0, making the installer treat Clack cancellation as success:

  ```console
  $ sed -n '27,31p' /tmp/oc-base/dist/onboard-helpers-DxyrQbNM.js
  function guardCancel(value, runtime) {
  if (isCancel(value)) {
  cancel(stylePromptTitle("Setup cancelled.") ?? "Setup cancelled.");
  runtime.exit(0);
  throw new Error("unreachable");
  ```

  **After (patched):** `guardCancel` exits with 130 (SIGINT convention), which the installer detects and aborts:

  ```console
  $ sed -n '27,31p' /tmp/wt-76386/dist/onboard-helpers-D47vq5rt.js
  function guardCancel(value, runtime) {
  if (isCancel(value)) {
  cancel(stylePromptTitle("Setup cancelled.") ?? "Setup cancelled.");
  runtime.exit(130);
  throw new Error("unreachable");
  ```

  **Install script `run_doctor` now detects exit 130:**

  ```console
  $ grep -n 'doctor_exit.*130\|abort_install_int' /tmp/wt-76386/scripts/install.sh
  35:abort_install_int() {
  47:trap abort_install_int INT
  2835:    if (( doctor_exit == 130 )); then
  2836:        abort_install_int
  3303:            if (( doctor_exit == 130 )); then
  ```

  **Doctor runs correctly on the live deployment:**

  ```console
  $ cd /tmp/wt-76386 && timeout 5 node openclaw.mjs doctor --non-interactive
  OPENCLAW
  OpenClaw doctor
  Doctor warnings
    - Left migrated plugin install index in place because archive already exists
  [state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
    - Left migrated plugin install index in place
  $ echo "exit code: $?"
  exit code: 0
  ```

  **Gateway starts cleanly with the patched module:**

  ```console
  $ timeout 10 node openclaw.mjs gateway
  [gateway] http server listening (9 plugins; 1.0s)
  [gateway] ready
  [shutdown] completed cleanly in 77ms
  ```

  **SIGINT during install triggers clean abort:**

  ```console
  $ set -m; (bash scripts/install.sh --no-onboard --no-prompt 2>&1) & PID=$!; sleep 2; kill -INT -- -$PID; wait $PID; echo "exit=$?"
  Preparing installer interface...
    OpenClaw Installer
  Detected: macos
  [1/3] Preparing environment
  Node.js found
  [2/3] Installing OpenClaw
  ! Installation interrupted
  exit=130
  ```

  **All 49 install script tests pass:**

  ```console
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts
   ✓ |tooling| install-sh.test.ts (49 tests) 4056ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  49 passed (49)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The compiled production code at `dist/onboard-helpers-D47vq5rt.js:30` calls `runtime.exit(130)` instead of `runtime.exit(0)` when the user cancels at a Clack prompt. The install script at line 2835 detects `doctor_exit == 130` and calls `abort_install_int`, which exits with 130 and the "Installation interrupted" message. Terminal output confirms: (1) doctor runs correctly on the live deployment, (2) SIGINT during install triggers clean abort with exit 130, (3) the gateway loads the patched module without errors.
- **What was not tested:** Live interactive Ctrl+C at a real Clack upgrade-doctor prompt (requires a state where doctor triggers an interactive migration question). The exit code propagation from `guardCancel(130)` through `run_doctor` to `abort_install_int` was verified via the compiled bundle, install script grep, and the 49-test suite.

target.title: feat(whatsapp): add replyToOfflineMessages config to process missed messages after reconnect
target.body:
## Problem

Messages received during WhatsApp disconnects are **silently lost**. When the gateway reconnects, offline messages arrive with `upsert.type === "append"` (history sync) and are **skipped** by default.

This causes:
- DM messages lost after reconnect
- Group messages stop working after gateway restart
- Blue ticks sent but no reply (sender sees message read but ignored)

**15+ issues** trace back to the same `append` skip.

## Solution

Add opt-in config to process offline messages:

```json5
{
  channels: {
    whatsapp: {
      replyToOfflineMessages: true,
      offlineMessageMaxAgeSeconds: 300, // default: 300 (5 minutes)
    },
  },
}
```

- `replyToOfflineMessages: true` — Process offline messages instead of skipping
- `offlineMessageMaxAgeSeconds: 300` — Skip messages older than 5 minutes (prevent flooding)

## Related Issues

- **#50093** — WhatsApp: Backfill missed messages after reconnection
- **#66904** — Support WhatsApp history sync on reconnect (closed as duplicate)
- **#19856** — Messages lost after 408 reconnect
- **#1619** — Messages lost during disconnect
- **#18672** — Messages dropped after prekey renegotiation
- **#1952, #2767, #20952** — Group messages stop after restart
- **#14069** — Group messages stop after relinking

## Based On

This PR is based on **#21719** by @faahim which was closed by stale bot due to inactivity.

The original PR had:
- ✅ Complete solution
- ✅ Tests passing
- ✅ Docs updated
- ✅ 15+ issues identified

## Changes

1. `src/config/types.whatsapp.ts` — Add config fields
2. `extensions/whatsapp/src/accounts.ts` — Add resolved fields
3. `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/monitor.ts` — Implement logic
4. `extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor.ts` — Pass options

## Default Behavior

**Unchanged** — By default, offline messages are still skipped (`replyToOfflineMessages: false`). Users must opt-in to process them.

---

**Context:** OpenClaw WhatsApp bundled user since 2026.3.13, currently on latest version.

target.title: feat(hooks): add persistent hook session mode
target.body:
## Summary Revives the persistent hook-session work from the stale/closed #27193 against current `main`. Adds an explicit `sessionMode: "isolated" | "persistent"` option for hook-agent runs so webhook integrations with stable, scoped `sessionKey` values can opt into multi-turn transcript reuse. Fixes #11665. ## Why Current hook-agent dispatch still routes direct `/hooks/agent` calls and mapped hook actions through the isolated cron-style runner. Even when callers provide the same `sessionKey`, that path passes `forceNew: true`, so OpenClaw creates a fresh session id and loses conversation history on every webhook invocation. Issue #11665 now spells out essentially the same narrow fix as #27193: keep the existing default isolation, but expose an explicit persistent mode for trusted hook threads. We have also been running this behavior in production for months on our shel-oodle OpenClaw instance. That production branch carried the same `sessionMode` behavior while tracking upstream releases, including the later hooks request-handler refactor. ## What changed - Adds `sessionMode` to hook mapping config/types/schema and generated config metadata. - Accepts `sessionMode` on direct `/hooks/agent` payloads. - Threads `sessionMode` through mapping resolution, transform results, replay dedupe scope, and hook dispatch. - Changes `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn` so only explicit `sessionMode: "persistent"` hook-agent runs avoid `forceNew` and can reuse a fresh stored session id. - Documents the security model: `isolated` remains the default; persistent mode should only be used with trusted integrations and scoped `sessionKey` values. Existing request `sessionKey` and prefix policy checks are unchanged. ## Compatibility / security - Default behavior is unchanged: omitted `sessionMode` behaves as `"isolated"` and creates a fresh session per hook dispatch. - Cron isolation remains unchanged unless the hook dispatch explicitly passes `sessionMode: "persistent"`. - Existing `hooks.allowRequestSessionKey` and `hooks.allowedSessionKeyPrefixes` checks still gate externally supplied or templated session keys. - Idempotency replay scope includes `sessionMode`, so different lifecycle modes are not conflated. ## Variance from #11665 spec None known. This implements the requested `sessionMode: "isolated" | "persistent"` surface for direct `/hooks/agent`, hook mappings, and transform results while preserving default isolation. ## Real behavior proof - **Behavior or issue addressed:** Hook-agent dispatch now supports explicit persistent hook sessions while preserving isolated default behavior. - **Real environment tested:** Live `shel-oodle-1` OpenClaw gateway, running `v2026.6.1` from this PR branch at `e4bce7737e128e72655a4c388a4ebed66e3b2053`. This proof used a real Fizzy webhook integration, real gateway/proxy services, a real persistent hook mapping, the real stored OpenClaw session store, and a real `gpt-5.5` Codex harness run. Secrets, account ids, SGIDs, and nonessential user/account fields are redacted below. - **Live services during proof:** ```console openclaw-gateway.service active (running) fizzy-webhook.service active (running) cloudflared.service active (running) Gateway version: OpenClaw 2026.6.1 (e4bce77) ``` - **Live webhook delivery proof:** A real Fizzy Playground card (`#1217`) generated real webhook events. The local Fizzy proxy accepted the signed events and forwarded them to the OpenClaw gateway with HTTP 200. ```console Jun 05 01:59:11 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T05:59:11.836Z] info: Fizzy webhook: card_published Jun 05 01:59:11 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T05:59:11.874Z] info: Forwarded to gateway: 200 Jun 05 02:00:10 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T06:00:10.288Z] info: Fizzy webhook: comment_created Jun 05 02:00:10 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T06:00:10.436Z] info: Forwarded to gateway: 200 Jun 05 02:00:35 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T06:00:35.329Z] info: Fizzy webhook: comment_created Jun 05 02:00:35 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T06:00:35.482Z] info: Forwarded to gateway: 200 Jun 05 02:00:50 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T06:00:50.276Z] info: Fizzy webhook: comment_created Jun 05 02:00:50 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T06:00:50.417Z] info: Forwarded to gateway: 200 ``` - **Persistent session reuse proof:** The same stable hook `sessionKey` reused the same stored OpenClaw `sessionId` and native Codex `threadId` across separate webhook invocations for card `#1217`. ```console # first live webhook turn, card_created/card_published type=session.started ts=2026-06-05T05:59:15.128Z sessionId=b99c7c98-2271-4af9-96f3-8f8a1bc4113a sessionKey=agent:fizzy-orchestrator:hook:fizzy:card-1217 threadId=019e965d-439c-7821-93c5-73f4e521e2ee provider=openai modelId=gpt-5.5 # later live webhook turn, user comment/@mention type=session.started ts=2026-06-05T06:00:36.552Z sessionId=b99c7c98-2271-4af9-96f3-8f8a1bc4113a sessionKey=agent:fizzy-orchestrator:hook:fizzy:card-1217 threadId=019e965d-439c-7821-93c5-73f4e521e2ee provider=openai modelId=gpt-5.5 # follow-up webhook generated by Sheldon's own Fizzy comment type=session.started ts=2026-06-05T06:00:53.300Z sessionId=b99c7c98-2271-4af9-96f3-8f8a1bc4113a sessionKey=agent:fizzy-orchestrator:hook:fizzy:card-1217 threadId=019e965d-439c-7821-93c5-73f4e521e2ee provider=openai modelId=gpt-5.5 ``` - **Real model/tool execution proof:** The first live turn reached the model and attempted the requested card-context command. It failed because the deployed environment did not have the helper command on `PATH`; this is useful proof that the persistent hook session reached real agent/tool execution rather than a mocked runner. ```console type=tool.call ts=2026-06-05T05:59:25.483Z sessionId=b99c7c98-2271-4af9-96f3-8f8a1bc4113a sessionKey=agent:fizzy-orchestrator:hook:fizzy:card-1217 provider=openai modelId=gpt-5.5 command=/bin/bash -lc 'fizzy-context 1217' type=tool.result ts=2026-06-05T05:59:25.500Z status=failed exitCode=127 output=/bin/bash: line 1: fizzy-context: command not found ``` - **Real same-thread response proof:** A later real comment webhook reused the same persistent session and the agent posted back to the same Fizzy card thread. [redacted mention] Confirmed, I received the reply on card #1217 and am posting back into the same Fizzy thread.

' type=tool.result ts=2026-06-05T06:00:50.328Z status=completed exitCode=0 output={"success":true,"data":{"body":{"plain_text":"[redacted mention] Confirmed, I received the reply on card #1217 and am posting back into the same Fizzy thread."},"card":{"url":"https://app.fizzy.do/[redacted]/cards/1217"},"creator":{"name":"Sheldon"},"url":"https://app.fizzy.do/[redacted]/cards/1217/comments/[redacted]"}} ``` - **Gateway lifecycle proof:** The gateway ran the live hook agent with the expected provider/model after the config repair and reported successful completion for the later persistent hook turns. ```console Jun 05 02:00:13 shel-oodle node[554078]: [diagnostic] lane wait exceeded: lane=session:agent:fizzy-orchestrator:hook:fizzy:card-1217 waitedMs=3223 queueAhead=0 activeAhead=1 activeNow=0 queueBehind=0 Jun 05 02:00:13 shel-oodle node[554078]: [agent/embedded] selected agent harness: provider=openai model=gpt-5.5 harness=codex requested=- runtimeOverride=- Jun 05 02:00:14 shel-oodle node[554078]: [diagnostic] message processed: channel=cron chatId=unknown messageId=unknown sessionId=b99c7c98-2271-4af9-96f3-8f8a1bc4113a sessionKey=agent:fizzy-orchestrator:hook:fizzy:card-1217 outcome=error duration=59941ms error="fizzy-context 1217 failed" Jun 05 02:00:17 shel-oodle node[554078]: [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement Jun 05 02:00:52 shel-oodle node[554078]: [agent/embedded] selected agent harness: provider=openai model=gpt-5.5 harness=codex requested=- runtimeOverride=- Jun 05 02:00:53 shel-oodle node[554078]: [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement Jun 05 02:00:55 shel-oodle node[554078]: [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement ``` - **Default isolated proof:** The live proof above covers explicit persistent hook reuse in a real setup. Default omitted/isolated behavior remains covered by targeted tests that assert `forceNew: true` and distinct run-scoped session keys for repeated default isolated runs. ```console stdout | ../../src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-key-isolation.test.ts > runCronIsolatedAgentTurn isolated session identity > uses a run-scoped key for embedded isolated cron execution [diagnostic] message queued: sessionId=isolated-run-1 sessionKey=agent:default:cron:daily-monitor:run:isolated-run-1 source=cron-isolated queueDepth=1 sessionState=idle [diagnostic] message processed: channel=cron chatId=unknown messageId=unknown sessionId=isolated-run-1 sessionKey=agent:default:cron:daily-monitor:run:isolated-run-1 outcome=completed duration=244ms stdout | ../../src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-key-isolation.test.ts > runCronIsolatedAgentTurn isolated session identity > keeps embedded isolated cron prompt-cache affinity stable across run sessions [diagnostic] message queued: sessionId=isolated-run-a sessionKey=agent:default:cron:daily-monitor:run:isolated-run-a source=cron-isolated queueDepth=1 sessionState=idle [diagnostic] message queued: sessionId=isolated-run-b sessionKey=agent:default:cron:daily-monitor:run:isolated-run-b source=cron-isolated queueDepth=1 sessionState=idle ✓ |cron| ../../src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-key-isolation.test.ts > runCronIsolatedAgentTurn isolated session identity > uses a run-scoped key for embedded isolated cron execution 476ms ✓ |cron| ../../src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-key-isolation.test.ts > runCronIsolatedAgentTurn isolated session identity > keeps embedded isolated cron prompt-cache affinity stable across run sessions 137ms ``` - **Observed result after fix:** Persistent hook mode reused the same real stored session and native Codex thread across multiple real webhook deliveries, and a later hook turn posted a real same-card Fizzy comment. target.body:
## Summary
- Preserve unresolved Google Chat `serviceAccountRef` as an error instead of silently falling back to legacy inline `serviceAccount` credentials.
- Add regression coverage for mixed `serviceAccountRef` + inline `serviceAccount` config.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Google Chat credential resolution must honor documented SecretRef precedence. A config with both `serviceAccountRef` and inline `serviceAccount` must fail closed when the ref is unresolved, and a resolved runtime snapshot must remove the sibling ref before Google Chat reads credentials.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw PR worktree on the rebased head `ef2bfcd48f`, using Node/pnpm from the repo environment. I checked env and `~/.profile` for Google Chat service-account material without printing values; none was present, so this uses redacted service-account JSON through the production Google Chat account resolver plus runtime SecretRef assignment/resolution paths.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran `pnpm exec tsx` against `extensions/googlechat/src/accounts.ts` and `extensions/googlechat/src/secret-contract.ts`, invoking `resolveGoogleChatAccount`, `collectRuntimeConfigAssignments`, `resolveSecretRefValues`, and `applyResolvedAssignments` with a mixed ref-plus-inline Google Chat config and a resolved env SecretRef snapshot.

**Evidence after fix:** Redacted terminal output from the production-path proof command:

```text
real-behavior-proof: googlechat SecretRef precedence
credential availability check: no GOOGLE_CHAT_* service-account env/profile entries were present; proof uses redacted service-account JSON through production resolver paths
mixed ref-plus-inline: FAIL_CLOSED
mixed ref-plus-inline error: channels.googlechat.accounts.default.serviceAccount: unresolved SecretRef "file:filemain:/channels/googlechat/missing-service-account". Resolve this command against an active gateway runtime snapshot before reading it.
mixed ref-plus-inline inline fallback used: false
resolved snapshot assignments: channels.googlechat.accounts.prod.serviceAccount

```

**Observed result after fix:** The stale mixed `serviceAccountRef` plus inline `serviceAccount` case failed closed before inline fallback, and the resolved snapshot path produced an account with the redacted resolved service-account email, removed `serviceAccountRef`, and did not use the legacy inline email.

**What was not tested:** A live Google Chat API send/webhook with real service-account credentials was not tested because this machine did not expose Google Chat credentials. The exercised paths are the production Google Chat credential resolver and runtime SecretRef resolver, not mocked test-only helpers.

## Maintainer compatibility note
This intentionally keeps the documented fail-closed precedence: when `serviceAccountRef` is present but unresolved, Google Chat does not fall back to inline `serviceAccount`, even if the inline credentials are otherwise valid. Existing stale mixed configs must repair/remove the stale ref or resolve it successfully.

target.title: fix(android): preserve numeric invoke error codes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android parses gateway invoke failures from `CODE: message` strings so the UI can preserve stable error codes. The parser only accepted uppercase letters and underscores, so valid Android/gateway codes containing digits, such as `A2UI_HOST_UNAVAILABLE`, were downgraded to `UNAVAILABLE` and shown/classified as generic failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway and Android node errors already use canonical uppercase codes that can include digits. This change keeps the existing strict parser shape but allows digits alongside uppercase letters and underscores.

## User Impact

Android users now see the specific A2UI/gateway error code instead of a generic unavailable error when the code contains a numeric component.

## Evidence

- `JAVA_HOME='F:\Program Files\Android\Android Studio\jbr' ANDROID_HOME='F:\Android\Sdk' ANDROID_SDK_ROOT='F:\Android\Sdk' GRADLE_OPTS='-Xmx1g -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8' ./gradlew.bat --no-daemon :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.gateway.InvokeErrorParserTest --console=plain`

## Summary

Extend the subagent yield-pause fix from [6f3b5f86](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6f3b5f8666f3a3877b62d9019b8842455fdf62e1) to top-level (non-subagent) sessions.

When a main session ends via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner already emits a lifecycle event with `yielded: true` and `livenessState: "paused"`. The runner's terminal lifecycle metadata, the agent-job snapshot cache, and the agent.wait dedupe entry all propagate those flags generically, so subagent and non-subagent runs benefit equally from those parts of 6f3b5f86.

The gap is in `gateway/session-lifecycle-state.ts`. `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` does not look at the `yielded` flag, so the session entry is persisted with `status: \"done\"` even though the runner has queued a post-yield continuation that drains on the next turn. Dashboards, restart recovery, and follow-up turns then treat the session as finished and race the continuation, producing the in-context overflow and out-of-order events the user reports.

## Why the same fix needs to apply to the top-level session

The subagent registry tracks active subagent runs in memory and uses `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` to keep yielded entries in a paused state instead of marking them complete. The main session has no equivalent in-memory registry; its lifecycle state is persisted directly through `persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` into the on-disk session entry. The gap shows up in three places:

1. The persisted session entry says `status: \"done\"`, so `sessions_list`, `sessions.changed` broadcasts, and dashboard UI all show the session as finished.
2. `main-session-restart-recovery` is keyed off `entry.abortedLastRun` and `entry.status === \"running\"`. With status=done it leaves the entry alone, but on a clean restart-mid-yield the yielded session can also end up `abortedLastRun=true` (the cleaned-lock path), at which point recovery would force a `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted...` resume that races the queued continuation.
3. A new user message arrives at a session that is internally paused but externally \"done\" — the gateway dispatches a fresh agent.run, and the queued steered yield-interrupt drains alongside the new user input, producing out-of-order assistant text.

## Shape of the change

- Recognize the lifecycle `yielded` flag in `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` and derive `status: \"paused\"` with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` instead of `done`. Yielded short-circuits before the `aborted`/`stopReason` branches so partial classifications cannot mask the paused state.
- Clear `pauseReason` on the next lifecycle `start` event so a fresh run reactivates the session, mirroring how `subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` clears `pauseReason` on completion.
- Add `\"paused\"` to `SessionRunStatus` in both `gateway/session-utils.types.ts` and `agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts`, and add `pauseReason?: \"sessions_yield\"` to `SessionEntry` and `GatewaySessionRow`.
- Surface `pauseReason` on the `sessions.changed` broadcast snapshot and the `loadGatewaySessionRow` builder so consumers (UI, sessions_list tool) see the paused state.
- Tighten `isTerminalSessionStatus` so the type predicate stays accurate after \"paused\" joins the union (paused is not terminal).
- Skip `main-session-restart-recovery` for entries with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` so they are not re-prompted with the generic interrupted-turn message.

The runner-level changes (yieldDetected -> livenessState=paused/yielded=true) and the gateway agent-job/agent-wait-dedupe propagation that 6f3b5f86 already added are unchanged. This PR plugs the missing seam between those generic signals and the persisted session entry.

## Test coverage

- `src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts`:
  - `marks yielded lifecycle end events as paused with sessions_yield reason` (persisted patch).
  - `treats yielded as paused even when aborted is set` (yield short-circuit).
  - `clears pauseReason when a fresh run starts on a paused session` (start-phase reactivation).
  - Existing terminal-mapping tests updated to include explicit `pauseReason: undefined` on non-yield ends.
- `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts`:
  - `skips sessions paused via sessions_yield instead of forcing a resume`.
  - `does not mark sessions with sessions_yield pauseReason as restart-aborted from cleaned locks`.

## Local validation

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts src/config/sessions.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.create-event.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent-wait-dedupe.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-output.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — all green (235 tests).
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm check:changelog-attributions` — all clean on changed files.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on \`fix(agents): pause yielded main-session runs\`.
- [ ] Manual smoke: trigger `sessions_yield` from a main-session conversation; confirm the session entry persists `status: paused` and `pauseReason: sessions_yield`, and that a follow-up turn flips back to `running` with `pauseReason: undefined`.
- [ ] Restart-recovery smoke: kill the gateway while a main session is paused via yield; confirm restart-recovery skips it instead of re-prompting with the interrupted-turn message.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Before this PR, when a top-level (non-subagent) embedded `openclaw` run ended via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner emitted `yielded=true` and `livenessState=paused` but the gateway treated it as a clean completion and wrote `status=done`. The session displayed as finished while awaiting a queued post-yield continuation, racing dashboards, restart-recovery, and follow-up turns. After this PR, the lifecycle persistence derives `status=paused` with `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, restart-recovery skips paused sessions, and `SessionRunStatus` adds `"paused"` so consumers can distinguish a yielded run from a completed one.
- **Real environment tested**: live OpenClaw gateway on rh-bot.lan, pid 65734, build SHA 23804e610c (upgrade-v2026.5.28 with this PR cherry-picked). The deployed `dist/server-chat-*.js` and `dist/main-session-restart-recovery-*.js` chunks carry the new `pauseReason`/`sessions_yield` logic; the proof script imports and executes those exact bundle bytes.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  # On rh-bot.lan, confirm deployed bundles carry the PR logic:
  grep -c 'sessions_yield\|pauseReason' \
    /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js
  # -> 1 (the new shouldSkipMainRecovery branch)

  grep -c 'sessions_yield\|pauseReason' \
    /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js
  # -> non-zero (new deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot branches)

  # Drive the deployed code with three scenarios:
  node /tmp/proof-75662-amittell.mjs
  ```
  Proof script (`/tmp/proof-75662-amittell.mjs`) extracts the deployed
  `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` from `server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js` via
  `vm.runInContext`, dynamically imports `main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js`
  to grab the exported `markRestartAbortedMainSessions`, seeds a temp
  state-dir with one yielded and one non-yielded `running` entry, and asserts
  three behaviors:
  1. Lifecycle `phase=end` with `yielded=true` -> `status=paused`,
     `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, `abortedLastRun=false`.
  2. Same entry passed to restart-recovery is SKIPPED (no `abortedLastRun`
     write, `updatedAt` unchanged).
  3. Sibling running entry without `pauseReason` is marked
     `abortedLastRun=true` (existing behavior preserved).
  Plus a guard check: lifecycle `phase=error` with `yielded=true` returns
  `status=failed` with NO `pauseReason` leak.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  === PR #75662 real-behavior proof ===
  host=rh-bot.lan pid=84884 node=v25.8.2
  dist=/Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist

  [1] lifecycle bundle: /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js
  [1a] yielded terminal -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"paused","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false,"pauseReason":"sessions_yield"}
  [1a] OK: paused status carries pauseReason=sessions_yield
  [1b] non-yielded terminal -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"done","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false}
  [1b] OK: non-yielded run preserves status=done with no pauseReason
  [1c] error+yielded -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"failed","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false}
  [1c] OK: error phase masks yielded marker, no pauseReason leak

  [2] seeded /var/folders/cn/.../state/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
  [2] recovery bundle: /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js
  [2] exports: i, n, r, t
  [main-session-restart-recovery] marked 1 interrupted main session(s) for restart recovery (pr-75662-proof)
  [2] mark result: {"marked":1,"skipped":1}
  [2] yielded entry after: {"sessionId":"sess-yielded","status":"running","pauseReason":"sessions_yield","startedAt":...,"updatedAt":1780285519789}
  [2] normal entry after:  {"sessionId":"sess-normal","status":"running","startedAt":...,"updatedAt":1780285521266,"abortedLastRun":true}
  [2a] OK: yielded session was skipped (no abortedLastRun, no updatedAt bump)
  [2b] OK: non-yielded running session was marked abortedLastRun=true

  === ALL PROOFS PASSED ===
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: All three scenarios pass on the deployed bundle. A yielded terminal event produces `status=paused`/`pauseReason=sessions_yield` and is skipped by restart recovery (no `abortedLastRun` mutation, no `updatedAt` bump). A non-yielded terminal event still produces `status=done` with no `pauseReason` (existing behavior preserved). An error phase masks the `yielded` flag and reports `status=failed` with no `pauseReason` leak, matching the gating comment in `resolveTerminalStatus`.
- **Targeted tests**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts` -> 22 passed + 15 passed (37/37). Broader: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts` -> 172/172 passed. `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --only=core --threads=4` -> clean.
- **What was not tested**: End-to-end live channel trigger (sending a real Telegram message that drives `sessions_yield` to completion); this is exercised by the existing vitest coverage in `pi-embedded-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` rather than reproduced live on rh-bot.


## Live exact-head capture (2026-06-12): found and fixed an emit-side gap

Running the requested live scenario on an isolated sandbox gateway (loopback :28795, fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, Control UI webchat, native `openai-completions` lane with a tool-calling model) surfaced a real defect in this PR's original head: **the paused state never persisted in live runs, on any lane.** A store probe polling every 0.3s across four real `sessions_spawn` + `sessions_yield` turns at head `be96a422ff` captured the persisted row going `running -> killed` with `abortedLastRun: true` at yield time -- the exact pre-PR failure this PR exists to prevent.

**Root cause (probe-instrumented):** `sessions_yield` aborts the attempt mid-stream (`runAbortController.abort("sessions_yield")`), and the terminal lifecycle event can be emitted from the abort teardown before `run.ts` post-processing writes the `yielded` meta. The bundle-level instrumentation captured the failing ordering directly:

```
emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = undefined  aborted = false   <- event emitted first
meta.yielded set -> false                                          <- run.ts wrote 551ms later
```

The event reaches `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` carrying `aborted` without `yielded`, and `resolveTerminalStatus` correctly resolves killed. The projection/recovery/UI logic this PR adds was never the problem; the emit side never fed it. The unit tests passed because they fabricate events that already carry `yielded: true`.

**Fix (in `a46ba508b8`):** `onYield` now records `yielded` through the subscription's terminal lifecycle meta channel at tool time, before the abort, using the same late-binding pattern the yield abort itself uses (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`). A regression test pins the handler half: an end event with `state.yielded` set and `aborted` resolved from the `isTerminalAborted` fallback still carries `yielded` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.test.ts`).

**Post-fix live proof, end to end (same sandbox, instrumented bundle):**

```
10:27:40.065  [PROBE] meta.yielded set -> true              (onYield records at tool time)
10:27:40.423  [PROBE] emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = true   (event carries it)
10:27:4x      store: status=paused pauseReason=sessions_yield abortedLastRun=false
~10:28        Sessions Control UI: main session "Paused", subagent "Live"
10:28:1x      gateway KILLED while paused -> store unchanged (paused, ab=false)
10:28:3x      gateway restarted -> recovery skips the paused session;
              no "[System] Your previous turn was interrupted" prompt in the chat
10:29:20      subagent (orphan-recovered post-restart) completes -> announce drains
              the queued continuation in order -> running, pauseReason cleared
10:30:48      continuation finishes -> done, abortedLastRun=false
```

Reproduced again on a second pass (store probe `paused/sessions_yield` at 15:54-15:56 with closure-identity probes confirming the onYield-time recording). This covers all three asks: visible Paused state, restart skip, and orderly continuation, captured live at the exact head plus the one-commit fix.

**Codex lane now covered too (was a sibling-lane gap, now fixed in this PR).** The Codex app-server harness lane emits its own terminal lifecycle event (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts` `emitLifecycleTerminal`) and was dropping the yield meta: the `phase:"end"` event carried only `phase`/`aborted`, never `yielded`, so the shared projection (`resolveYielded`) persisted Codex-backed yields as done/killed. The fix forwards `{yielded, livenessState:"paused", stopReason:"end_turn"}` on that event when `result.yieldDetected`, exactly as the native runner does, gated on the flag the `sessions_yield` tool already sets via `onYield -> onYieldDetected`. The Codex lifecycle event flows through the same `onAgentEvent -> server-chat -> persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent -> resolveYielded` path as the native lane.

Proven live on the Codex lane: a real `openai/gpt-5.5` turn through the Codex app-server (ChatGPT OAuth) that calls `sessions_yield` now persists `status=paused`, `pauseReason=sessions_yield` (was `done` pre-fix), and the subagent then drains the queued continuation in order back to `done`. An integration test (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.yield-lifecycle.test.ts`) asserts the Codex lifecycle end event carries `yielded:true`/`livenessState:"paused"`/`stopReason:"end_turn"` on yield and omits them on a normal turn (verified red without the fix).

Codex protocol behavior checked against the sibling `../codex` source (HEAD `b8aea2340`): `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/ServerRequest.ts:19` defines the `{ "method": "item/tool/call", id, params: DynamicToolCallParams }` app-server -> client request, which is how the app-server invokes the OpenClaw `sessions_yield` dynamic tool (setting `yieldDetected`); turn lifecycle requests (`turn/start`/`turn/steer`/`turn/interrupt`) are at `ClientRequest.ts:90`. This change adds no new protocol dependency -- it forwards an OpenClaw-side flag onto OpenClaw's own lifecycle event.

target.title: Recover stranded message-tool finals by default
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #85714 for the direct/source-channel failure where an agent turn can finish successfully with a substantive final answer, but the user sees nothing because the channel is in `message_tool_only` visible-reply mode and the model skipped `message(action=send)`.

This supersedes #88992. I kept the useful shape from that PR: substantive-final detection, room-event and send-policy guards, a one-shot retry marker, message-tool retry, collect isolation, deferred drain, QA coverage, and clearer prompt wording. The replacement removes the new `messages.strandedReplyRecovery` opt-in surface so guarded recovery is the default for the specific stranded-final class.

## Why This Change Was Made

The July 3 Telegram repro is not a broad final-fallback problem; it is a silent-success problem. In `message_tool_only`, final assistant text is intentionally private, but a substantive final with no message-tool delivery should not end the user-visible source turn as if everything succeeded.

The fix now:

- warns only through the existing substantive private-final predicate;
- skips `room_event`, `sendPolicyDenied`, successful source delivery, short/silent finals, and explicit silence;
- enqueues exactly one retry marked `stranded-reply-retry`;
- applies that recovery to both direct source turns and queued followup turns;
- prepends that retry ahead of already queued follow-ups, protects it from old-item overflow eviction, drains it before overflow summaries, and uses the refreshed follow-up runner;
- stores retry identity in private queued-run metadata rather than user-controlled summary text;
- forces that retry out of collect batching and suppresses retry prompt persistence;
- asks the model to deliver the sanitized visible reply via `message(action=send)`;
- if enqueueing fails or the retry strands again, delivers only a marked sanitized diagnostic;
- suppresses that diagnostic only when the retry already delivered to the source chat through the message tool or internal source-reply path;
- never marks or auto-delivers the original private final text.

## User Impact

For users in Telegram/source-channel chats configured for tool-only visible replies, a substantive reply that previously disappeared should now either:

- recover through one visible `message(action=send)` retry, or
- show `I generated a reply but could not deliver it to this chat. Please try again.`

Intentional silence remains silent. Hidden reasoning, tool output, trace text, raw private finals, send-policy-denied text, room events, and short notes are not auto-published.


target.title: feat(tools/write): add append mode for agent writes
target.body:
## Summary

Revives and rebases the closed append-mode work from #75549 for the canonical data-loss issue #40001.

The `write` tool currently overwrites existing files. OpenClaw has an append-only wrapper for memory-flush runs, but ordinary agent turns, cron skills, and monitor-and-react workflows do not have a first-class append path. This PR adds a backwards-compatible optional `append: true` parameter to `write` so agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

When `append` is omitted or false, existing overwrite behavior is unchanged.

## What changed

- Adds optional `append?: boolean` handling for host/workspace and sandbox write operations.
- Preserves existing workspace/root guard behavior.
- Serializes concurrent appends through the existing file mutation queue.
- Preserves validation behavior for blank paths and invalid content.
- Surfaces sandbox I/O failures except for missing-file cases used to create-on-append.
- Honors aborted append calls before entering the mutation queue.
- Adds focused regression coverage for append-create, append-accumulate, append-false-overwrites, validation, and sandbox/workspace behavior.

## Validation

Run in an isolated checkout on current `origin/main`:

- `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.read.host-tilde-expansion.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.params.test.ts`
  - passed: `10 files / 170 tests`
- `git diff --check`
- `corepack pnpm lint:core`
  - passed: `0 warnings / 0 errors`

## Notes

This PR intentionally keeps the API small and backwards-compatible. It does not remove or relax the existing memory-flush append-only wrapper; it gives ordinary `write` callers an explicit append path instead of relying on prompt discipline or destructive read/concatenate/write patterns.

Fixes #40001.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** The agent write tool supports `append: true` without overwriting the existing file, while still using the workspace-root guard for workspace-only host writes.

target.title: feat(sessions): create concise titles for saved sessions
target.body:
Closes #77165
Related #89705

## What Problem This Solves

Users with many saved sessions only had manual names, first-message fallbacks, or session-id fallbacks, so session history was hard to scan and search.

This PR adds an opt-in path that stores a durable `autoTitle` once enough direct user turns exist, while keeping manual labels/display names/origin labels/subjects higher priority.

The intended result is that enabled sessions can show and search concise stored titles in the gateway and Control UI, without changing default behavior or requiring a migration/backfill.

Out of scope: manual rename UI, migration/backfill for existing sessions, default-enabling generated titles, provider/channel/plugin capability changes, agent-facing `sessions_list` behavior, ConfigIO typing, generic session-store merge policy, and test-project routing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The feature is implemented as a default-off `sessionTitle` config surface plus additive `autoTitle` session metadata. The privacy/cost boundary is explicit: title generation is default-off; when enabled, the background title task reads only direct user text from the transcript head, skips heartbeat, internal-system, tool-mediated, and media-only/textless records, caps each message and the total model input, and writes only if the persisted `sessionId` still matches.

The title lifecycle is kept at the session metadata source of truth: `autoTitle` is created once after a successful reply, persisted without refreshing `updatedAt`, cleared on reset/new/rollover, and projected to gateway and Control UI consumers. This avoids recomputing titles in display fallbacks and avoids making an older session look newly active when a delayed title write lands later.

Manual title sources remain authoritative, and the feature stays opt-in/default-off. Title generation runs only after reply delivery; failures log or no-op and do not block, retry, or change the user reply. The remaining product/privacy/auth-profile routing decisions are maintainer-owned because enabled sessions send bounded transcript excerpts to the selected title model.

## User Impact

When `sessionTitle.enabled` is true, users with many saved sessions can identify conversations by concise stored titles instead of first-message snippets or ids.

Default-off behavior is unchanged. Existing manual names still win over generated titles, reset/rollover clears generated metadata without removing manual names, and late background title writes do not reorder sessions by refreshing activity timestamps.

## Evidence

- **Fix classification:** Root-cause feature completion for opt-in model-created session titles.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the scoped code update after focused validation and local real gateway proof; maintainer product/privacy/auth acceptance remains maintainer-owned before merge.
- **Root cause:** Saved sessions had no durable generated-title source of truth, so session lists fell back to manual names, first user message snippets, or session ids.
- **Control UI display follow-up:** Browser proof showed the sessions table could filter by `autoTitle` but did not render an `autoTitle`-only row title; the table now shows `autoTitle` as the visible secondary title only when no manual label/display name exists.

- **Why this is root-cause fix:** `autoTitle` is created once in the reply lifecycle, stored on the session entry, preserved without refreshing session activity, cleared with reset/rollover state, and projected to gateway/Control UI instead of being recomputed by display fallbacks.
- **Patch quality notes:** The broad catches are intentional isolation for a non-blocking background title task; failures log or no-op instead of interrupting the user reply. The `null`/`false` returns are explicit skip/no-title states for invalid, absent, stale, manually titled, or unreadable sessions.
- **What did NOT change:** No unrelated behavior, no default enablement, no migration/backfill, no manual rename UI, no channel/provider/plugin capability change, no agent-facing `sessions_list` behavior change, and no ConfigIO or generic session-store merge policy change.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `autoTitle` is persisted as session metadata and projected outward; gateway and UI do not maintain a second title source. Runtime auth selection for this path is kept behind internal runtime code so the public runtime-auth helper contract is not expanded.

## Summary
- Rebased this replacement lane onto latest `origin/main` and kept the minimal-test-gateway requester guard from the prior patch.

- Documented `openclaw/plugin-sdk/session-run-cancel-runtime` in `docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md`, including supported imports (`onSessionRunCancel`, `requestSessionRunCancel`, public types) and the explicit note that the core-owned emitter is not public.

target.title: feat(agents): composable termination algebra + GSAR grounding scorer
target.body:
Closes #77981

## What this does

Adds a **composable termination algebra** for A2A agent loops and implements **GSAR** (Typed Grounding for Hallucination Detection and Recovery) from [Kamelhar 2026, arxiv:2604.23366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23366) as a first-class `TerminationCondition`. Both ship as **standalone, composable primitives** (`src/agents/termination.ts`, `src/agents/gsar.ts`) with full unit + live-API coverage.

> **Scope (updated):** this PR is **library/groundwork only**. An earlier revision plumbed an optional `termination` param into the A2A ping-pong loop (`sessions-send-tool`), but no production caller selected it, so that hook was dead code — and gating real A2A message delivery on a reply-text-only GSAR scorer is a product/security decision. The dormant hook has been removed; wiring the policy through a real `sessions_send` entry point, with a trusted-evidence GSAR contract (retrieved sources, not self-tagged reply text), is deferred to an owner-reviewed follow-up.

---

## Proof 1 — the algebra saves turns

```
Task: "Where is the nearest coffee shop?"

WITHOUT algebra   MaxIterations(5)
  Claude  ▓▓▓▓▓  5 turns  (had the answer at turn 2, we waited anyway)
  GPT     ▓▓▓▓▓  5 turns

WITH algebra   TextMention("FOUND IT").or(MaxIterations(5))
  Claude  ▓▓░░░  2 turns  ← "Blue Bottle on Mission St. FOUND IT"  ✓ EXIT
  GPT     ▓▓▓▓▓  5 turns  ← never says FOUND IT → MaxIterations saves it

  saved: 3 turns = 60% less waiting for Claude
```

Claude naturally signals completion. GPT does not. The combinator captures this difference without any provider-specific code.

---

## Proof 2 — soft signals must be paired with a hard bound

```
soft_signal                        ✗  UNSAFE — may never stop
soft_signal.or(MaxIterations(N))   ✓  SAFE   — always terminates
```

Proven by the hallucinating-provider scenario: Claude never says DONE, GSAR score never reaches 0.80 — `MaxIterations` fires at turn 5 every time. Budget holds.

The AND combinator lets you guard against vague early answers:

```typescript
const detailed = new CustomCondition(s => [s.replyText.length >= 40, "detailed_enough"]);
const cond = new TextMention("FOUND IT").and(detailed).or(new MaxIterations(5));
// turn 1: "FOUND IT!" — too short, fails `detailed`
// turn 2: "Blue Bottle on Mission St, 4 min walk. FOUND IT" — passes both ✓
```

---

## Proof 3 — GSAR score formula (arxiv:2604.23366 §3.2)

```
        W(G) + W(K)
S = ─────────────────────────    ∈ [0, 1]
     W(G) + W(U) + ρ·W(X) + W(K)

G = grounded   U = ungrounded   X = contradicted   K = complementary
```

**6 structural properties proven in the suite:**

| Property | Statement |
|----------|-----------|
| P1 Boundedness | S ∈ [0,1] always |
| P2 Grounded monotonicity | U→G never decreases S |
| P3 Contradiction penalty | adding X never increases S |
| P4 Complementary value | K contributes but < equivalent G |
| P5 Non-suppression | X stays in denominator even at ρ=0 |
| P6 Asymmetry | w(inference) < w(tool_match) strictly decreases S |

---

## Proof 4 — GSAR decision tiers and threshold stability

```
score   0.0──────────0.65──────────0.80──────────1.0
              replan      regenerate      proceed
                                   ▲
                             τ_proceed = 0.80 sits on a
                             ≥85%-accuracy plateau across [0.75, 0.85]
                             not a cliff — safe to ship as default
```

`calibrateThresholds()` recovers the paper defaults from labeled examples. Sensitivity analysis proves all parameters vary monotonically — no cliff edges anywhere.

---

## Proof 5 — GSAR wired into a recovery loop

```typescript
// Algorithm 1 from the paper — bounded recovery, termination guaranteed
new GroundednessCondition(scorer).or(new MaxIterations(K_max))
```

| Provider type | Behavior | Turns used |
|---------------|----------|------------|
| Grounded (Claude-like) | exits at turn 1 | 80% reduction vs flat |
| Recovering | exits at first grounded reply (turn 3) | quality-gated, not time-gated |
| Hallucinating | never reaches proceed — MaxIterations saves it | budget holds |

---

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: A2A agent loops have only flat `MaxIterations` budgets, wasting turns when a provider has already produced a satisfactory answer or is actively hallucinating. This PR adds the reusable primitives that fix that — delivered as standalone library modules (`src/agents/termination.ts`, `src/agents/gsar.ts`), with the production `sessions_send` wiring deferred to an owner-reviewed follow-up: (a) a composable termination algebra (`TextMention`, `MaxIterations`, `CustomCondition`, `.and(...)`, `.or(...)`) so loops can exit on natural completion signals while keeping a hard upper bound; and (b) the GSAR (Typed Grounding) scorer from arxiv:2604.23366, exposed as `GroundednessCondition`, which partitions reply claims into `[G]/[U]/[X]/[K]` tags and exits the loop when the grounding score crosses the proceed threshold (default 0.80). The two compose: `new GroundednessCondition(scorer).or(new MaxIterations(K_max))` is the bounded-recovery pattern from the paper's Algorithm 1.
- **Real environment tested**: local Node v22.22.2 runtime against the real patched modules from this branch (`feat/gsar-termination-algebra` HEAD `4678e3ebaf`). target.title: fix(memory-core): drop dreaming theme echoes from promotion candidates
target.body:
## Summary

Light Sleep / Deep Sleep phases write
\`\`\`
- Theme: \`X\` kept surfacing across N memories.
\`\`\`
into daily notes. The next dreaming cycle re-ingests the first line as a fresh candidate before the indented \`status: staged\` and \`recalls: 0\` rows land. The 5-field contamination check (\`hasNarrativeLead && hasConfidence && hasEvidence && hasStatus && hasRecalls\`) then misses the snippet, so the theme echo gets promoted into MEMORY.md and the cycle keeps recursing. Real workspaces accumulate dozens of these per agent (verified by inspection of multiple `~/.openclaw/workspace-*/memory/2026-04-*.md` files).

This PR adds a separate guard: when a snippet has a narrative lead AND matches the unique \`kept surfacing across N memories\` signature, mark it as contaminated even without status/recalls. The original 5-field check stays as additional safety.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.test.ts` — 45 tests pass, including the new "treats Light Sleep theme echoes as contaminated even without status/recalls" case
- [x] `pnpm check:changed` — typecheck and tests green for extension lanes
- [x] Existing "does not treat ordinary candidate notes with daily-memory evidence as contaminated" still passes (regular candidates without the theme signature stay through)

## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:

If this PR fixes a plugin beta-release blocker, title it `fix(<plugin-id>): beta blocker - <summary>` and link the matching `Beta blocker: <plugin-name> - <summary>` issue labeled `beta-blocker`. Contributors cannot label PRs, so the title is the PR-side signal for maintainers and automation.

  - Problem: compaction and memory-flush bookkeeping could advance updatedAt, making legacy sessions without lifecycle timestamps look fresh across daily/idle reset boundaries.
  - Why it matters: stale session context could survive when OpenClaw should start a fresh session.
  - What changed: metadata-only compaction/flush writes now preserve activity timestamps, and regression tests lock daily/idle behavior.
  - What did NOT change (scope boundary): no reset policy rewrite, no store migration, no config/schema changes, no docs/changelog changes.

## Change Type (select all)

  - Missing detection / guardrail: there was no regression coverage for legacy rows missing sessionStartedAt /
    lastInteractionAt after metadata-only writes.
  - Contributing context (if known): updatedAt is still a legacy fallback for reset freshness when explicit lifecycle timestamps cannot be recovered.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

For bug fixes or regressions, name the smallest reliable test coverage that should catch this. Otherwise write `N/A`.

- Coverage level that should have caught this:

  - Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it tests the store merge seam plus the session reset decision without broad runner/e2e setup.
  - Existing test that already covers this (if any): existing reset and heartbeat tests covered related behavior, but not compaction/flush metadata writes against legacy rows.
  - If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

  Legacy sessions that should expire by daily or idle reset will now expire even if compaction or memory-flush metadata was written shortly before the next user message.

## Diagram (if applicable)

For UI changes or non-trivial logic flows, include a small ASCII diagram reviewers can scan quickly. Otherwise write `N/A`.

```text
  Before:
  [compaction/flush metadata] -> updatedAt refreshed -> legacy reset fallback sees fresh session

  After:
  [compaction/flush metadata] -> updatedAt preserved -> legacy reset fallback sees stale session -> reset
```

## Security Impact (required)

  - New permissions/capabilities? (No)
  - Secrets/tokens handling changed? (No)
  - New/changed network calls? (No)
  - Command/tool execution surface changed? (No)
  - Data access scope changed? (No)

### Steps

  1. Create a legacy session row missing sessionStartedAt; for idle, also missing lastInteractionAt.
  2. Persist compaction or memory-flush metadata after a reset boundary or inside the idle window.
  3. Send the next real user message through session initialization.

### Expected

  - The legacy session resets when daily or idle policy says it is stale.

### Actual

  - Before this fix, metadata writes could refresh updatedAt, causing stale legacy sessions to be treated as fresh.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

  - Verified scenarios: targeted session store, compaction bookkeeping, memory flush metadata, heartbeat reset guard, and legacy daily/idle reset regression tests.
  - Edge cases checked: default updateSessionStoreEntry still refreshes activity; preserve-activity path only applies to selected metadata callers; modern idle rows use lastInteractionAt.

target.title: fix(googlechat): preserve thread reply target through delivery
target.body: ## Summary - **Problem:** Google Chat replies could leave the inbound Chat thread and appear as new top-level messages. - **Why it matters:** delayed or tool-driven assistant replies break group-thread UX when they detach from the conversation the user spoke into. - **What changed:** preserve `message.thread.name` as `MessageThreadId`, expose it to reply/message-tool threading, and normalize Google Chat outbound thread targets before they reach `thread.name`. - **What did NOT change:** no Google Chat per-thread OpenClaw session isolation; core reply plumbing remains channel-agnostic and Google Chat resource-name handling stays behind the Google Chat boundary. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor required for the fix - [ ] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [ ] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [x] Integrations - [x] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Related #69422 - Related #39554 - [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Google Chat assistant replies from existing Chat threads should remain in the inbound thread. - Real environment tested: Linux VPS-hosted OpenClaw Google Chat runtime with service-account auth and a real Google Chat space. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: Jai sent real Google Chat threaded messages and confirmed assistant replies stayed in-thread before this PR was marked ready. - Evidence after fix: screenshot evidence is attached below: - Before: Google Chat reply appeared outside the inbound thread. - After: Google Chat reply stayed inside the inbound thread. - Scope note: typing-placeholder editing is separate follow-up behavior; this PR fixes thread placement. - Observed result after fix: live Google Chat replies stayed in-thread; local seam tests also verified natural replies, message-tool sends, and current-reply behavior use the inbound Google Chat thread resource. - What was not tested: every Google Chat account/space policy combination; typing-placeholder edit/cleanup for message-tool sends; Google Chat per-thread OpenClaw session isolation, which is out of scope. - Before evidence: prior behavior re-rooted replies as new top-level Chat messages. ## Root Cause (if applicable) - Root cause: Google Chat exposes different resource shapes for messages (`spaces/.../messages/...`) and threads (`spaces/.../threads/...`), and OpenClaw previously let message-shaped values flow into thread-routing seams. - Missing detection / guardrail: tests covered legacy single-resource channels, but not a provider where current message id and current thread id are different resource names. - Contributing context: - Inbound webhook context did not populate generic `MessageThreadId` from `message.thread.name`. - The message-tool path had no inbound-thread default when the agent omitted `threadId`. - `[[reply_to_current]]` resolves to the current message id; for Google Chat that value must be converted to the inbound thread before delivery. ## Regression Test Plan (if applicable) - Coverage level that should have caught this: - [x] Unit test - [x] Seam / integration test - [ ] End-to-end test - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient - Target test or file: - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-plumbing.test.ts` - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.test.ts` - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts` - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-delivery.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.webhook-routing.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/channel.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/actions.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts` - Scenario the test should lock in: Google Chat has a current message resource and a distinct current thread resource; implicit replies and message-tool sends use the thread resource, while message-shaped reply ids are rewritten or rejected before reaching the Chat API. - Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it covers webhook ingress, core reply seams, message-tool routing, channel delivery, and the API boundary without requiring live Google Chat in CI. - Existing test that already covers this (if any): none. - If no new test is added, why not: N/A. ## User-visible / Behavior Changes Google Chat assistant replies from an existing Chat thread now stay in that thread instead of creating a new top-level message. ## Diagram (if applicable) ```text Before: Google Chat webhook -> currentMessageId=spaces/.../messages/... -> delivery sends that as thread.name -> Chat API rejects/falls back -> new top-level thread After: Google Chat webhook -> MessageThreadId=spaces/.../threads/... -> reply/tool delivery resolves outbound thread -> Chat API receives thread.name=spaces/.../threads/... ``` ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? `No` - Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No` - New/changed network calls? `No` - Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` - Data access scope changed? `No` - If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS local checkout; Linux VPS-hosted runtime for real Chat verification - Runtime/container: OpenClaw source checkout; local verification on exact rebased head `a617644c81dd43bb7285d3001ca6d19750e62e68`; live Google Chat verification on a Linux VPS-hosted runtime with the thread-placement patch applied - Model/provider: N/A - Integration/channel (if any): Google Chat service-account auth - Relevant config (redacted): Google Chat enabled with group mention policy; no secret/config changes required ### Steps 1. Send a threaded Google Chat message that mentions the bot. 2. Let the assistant produce a normal final reply. 3. Exercise message-tool sends without explicit `threadId`. 4. Exercise `[[reply_to_current]]` behavior where the core seam supplies the current message id. ### Expected - Replies and message-tool sends stay in the original Google Chat thread. - Explicit thread-shaped ids are preserved. - Message-shaped or malformed thread targets never reach `thread.name` as-is. ### Actual - Before this patch: replies could re-root as new top-level Chat messages. - After this patch: live verification and local seam coverage keep replies in the inbound thread. - Scope note: typing-placeholder editing is separate follow-up behavior and is not fixed by this PR. ## Evidence - [x] Failing test/log before + passing after - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [x] Screenshot/recording - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) Screenshot evidence attached below: - Before screenshot: Google Chat reply escaped the inbound thread and appeared outside the original conversation thread. - After screenshot: Google Chat reply stayed inside the inbound thread. - Scope note: the after screenshot may still show a stale typing placeholder when the message-tool path is used; typing-placeholder edit/cleanup is not part of this PR.
